This paper examines the expressive power of constraint handling rules (crls) by analyzing the head, body, and resulting constraint stores. We demonstrate that whether a head contains one, two, or a greater number of atoms significantly influences the language's expressive capabilities. Furthermore, we provide a method to transform a constraint logic program (clp) into an equivalent crlo, and we establish that any clp can be converted to a crlo such that the resulting program's size is at most a linear multiple of the size of the original program.

We examine the orientation of galaxy spin within the redshift range $0.1 < z < 0.6$ using the SDSS-DR7, 2MASS, and WISE surveys. By analyzing the orientation of the spin axis relative to the dipole axis of the galaxy distribution, we identify a significant excess of galaxies with parallel axes. This dipole is robustly confirmed across all three datasets, with the spin direction dipole aligning closely with the galaxy distribution dipole. Furthermore, we investigate the correlation between the spin orientation and the galaxy position within the large-scale structure (LCSS). Our results indicate a significant excess of galaxies with parallel axes within $100\,h^{-1}\text{Mpc}$ of the LCSS, suggesting that galaxy spin directions are influenced by large-scale structures.

Few-shot learning (FSL) has emerged as a critical area of research, driven by the need to train models with limited labeled data. Although recent advances in metric learning have significantly boosted FSL performance, these methods often struggle with the computational cost of sampling and the prevalence of label noise. This paper introduces Eigen-Reptile, a novel approach that integrates Eigen-Centers into the traditional Reptile algorithm to mitigate these issues. By leveraging Eigen-Centers, Eigen-Reptile effectively reduces sampling overhead and enhances robustness against noisy labels. Empirical results on the miniImageNet and CIFAR-100 benchmarks demonstrate that Eigen-Reptile outperforms state-of-the-art methods, achieving improvements of 2.0% and 2.3% respectively. Furthermore, our analysis reveals that Eigen-Reptile exhibits greater resilience to label noise than its counterparts.

The Mini-Mental State Examination (MMSE) is a standard instrument for assessing cognitive impairment, yet its primary limitation is the reliance on subjective clinical judgments. Consequently, there is a critical need to develop objective, data-driven methods for predicting MMSE scores. This study introduces a deep learning framework designed to predict scores by analyzing raw EEG signals. We evaluated the model's performance using the public ADNI dataset, which contains EEG recordings from Alzheimer's disease patients and healthy controls. Our results demonstrate that the proposed method achieves a correlation coefficient of 0.75 between predicted and actual MMSE scores.

Ethical analysis is essential for the design and deployment of artificial intelligence. This study examines the prevailing literature on AI Ethics to identify methodologies for conducting such analysis. We critique the current state of AI Ethical literature, arguing that it is overly descriptive and fails to provide actionable guidance. We propose that the field must pivot toward a more prescriptive approach, grounded in the integration of normative ethics. Furthermore, we argue that the definition of "ethics" itself requires refinement to better align with the specific demands of the field.

The concept of a trio was originally proposed by McNaughton and Zaporożec in 1977 to characterize a trio of languages over finite words that is closed under union, intersection, and complementation. In this study, we broaden this definition to include infinite word languages. We demonstrate that the family of ω-regular languages constitutes the unique Boolean-complete full trio that decides on a decidable subset. This result is derived from a new finding: any Boolean-complete full trio of ω-words that is decidable must be regular.

This paper introduces a hybrid channel estimation framework designed for millimeter-wave (mmWave) communications, combining a low-complexity initial estimator with a deep neural network (DNN) to refine accuracy. The DNN is trained to forecast future channel impulse responses (CIRs) based on past and current channel state information (CSI) and the transmitted signal. Simulation outcomes demonstrate that this hybrid approach significantly outperforms conventional CSI prediction techniques.

Recent discrepancies between experimental results and Standard Model predictions for $V_{ud}$ and $V_{us}$ hint at physics beyond the Standard Model. This paper examines the impact of a scalar leptoquark on these discrepancies, specifically targeting a model designed to resolve the $(g-2)_\mu$ anomaly. We demonstrate that the viable parameter space for the leptoquark is severely restricted by constraints from $K^\pm \to \pi^\pm \nu\bar\nu$, $K_L \to \mu^+\mu^-$, and $K_{L,\mu3}$ experiments.

This study introduces a new network architecture designed for the simultaneous prediction of the six degrees of freedom (6DoF) pose and optical flow. The approach leverages convolutional layers with dilated kernels to capture scene context, thereby enhancing the performance of the optical flow estimation. The model is capable of processing multiple images at once, which further improves flow accuracy. Additionally, the system incorporates a self-supervised learning strategy to refine the network's output. Experimental results indicate that the network achieves superior performance compared to existing state-of-the-art methods.

Data views are frequently constructed by merging information from multiple sources, yet they often inadvertently expose private details belonging to specific sources. This paper proposes a method to disentangle private information from shared information by leveraging a generative adversarial network (GAN) to model private data as a byproduct of synthesizing shared data. This approach is conceptually grounded in the observation that private data can be reconstructed from the combined dataset. The proposed technique is evaluated on two distinct domains: natural images and text documents. In the visual domain, it successfully separates private information from background scenes, whereas in the textual domain, it achieves the separation of personally identifiable information from open-access research papers.

This study investigates the correlation between the hot dust emission in galaxies and their radio emission, utilizing a sample of 1,000 galaxies from the Herschel-ATLAS survey. The sample is divided into two groups: 400 galaxies with radio emission and 600 without. We analyze the hot dust emission at 160 $\mu$m alongside the radio flux at 1.4 GHz, comparing these against the total infrared luminosity ($L_{\rm IR}$) and the radio luminosity ($L_{\rm 1.4GHz}$). Our findings indicate that galaxies exhibiting hot dust emission are typically radio-luminous and display disturbed morphologies, whereas those lacking such emission tend to have quiescent structures. We observe a strong positive correlation between the ratio of hot dust luminosity to total infrared luminosity and the ratio of radio luminosity to infrared luminosity, a trend that persists even after accounting for the star formation rate. Furthermore, we examine the impact of galaxy morphology on this correlation, noting that while disturbed galaxies show a steeper relationship, quiescent galaxies display a flatter one. Additionally, we find that the hot dust-to-infrared luminosity ratio is higher in galaxies with a higher radio luminosity, regardless of their morphology. These outcomes suggest that hot dust emission is more prevalent in star-forming galaxies with disturbed morphologies, which are also the primary contributors to the radio emission.

Although recent advancements have significantly improved the moral reasoning capabilities of large language models (LLMs), these systems often struggle to comprehend the intricate reasoning processes humans employ when addressing ethical dilemmas. To bridge this gap, we introduce MORALCOT, a novel prompting technique designed to enhance LLMs' ability to grasp human moral logic. By leveraging the Chain-of-Thought (CoT) framework, MORALCOT guides models through a structured, step-by-step analysis of a specific case, breaking down moral judgments into finer components. Our experiments demonstrate that MORALCOT substantially boosts the performance of various LLMs on the Moral Judgment Benchmark (MJB), surpassing the results of other CoT-based approaches. Furthermore, we validate the method's effectiveness across multiple tasks, including moral prediction, moral classification, and moral question answering.

A valuation ring $V$ with a residue field $k$ of characteristic $p$ is expressible as the direct limit of valuation rings whose residue fields are strictly discrete, provided that $k$ is separably generated over its prime field.

The two-dimensional Dirac equation is fundamental to numerous domains, including condensed matter physics, graphene physics, and high-energy physics. This study introduces a numerical technique for solving the Dirac equation with an arbitrary potential, applicable to both bound states and scattering problems. The method's accuracy and computational efficiency are demonstrated through calculations of energy spectra for various potentials, as well as the computation of phase shifts and the determination of the S-matrix.

Model Predictive Control (MPC) has proven effective in various real-time applications, particularly in driving assistance and automation. This study introduces a cooperative MPC framework for automated vehicles, designed to optimize the performance of a platoon by leveraging the predictive capabilities of MPC alongside the optimization of a nonlinear cost function. The resulting framework is formulated as a constrained nonlinear optimal control problem, solved in real-time using the CasADi tool suite and the COVOPPO solver. The proposed approach is validated through simulations involving two-lane merging scenarios, demonstrating its efficacy in managing cooperative driving tasks.

The proliferation of social media has created a significant challenge regarding the reliability of information. This study investigates how social platforms influence users' credibility assessments of news. We examine the data from a survey of 1,000 participants, who evaluated the trustworthiness of 1,000 news articles on a scale of 1 to 5. The analysis demonstrates that social media signals, such as the number of likes and shares, serve as strong predictors of a news item's credibility. Furthermore, we developed a machine learning model that utilizes these social signals to forecast the trust ratings provided by individuals. This model achieved an accuracy of 70%, underscoring the critical role that social media plays in shaping a user's perception of what is credible.

The rise of the Internet of Vehicles (IoV) has enabled vehicles to share real-time data, such as traffic updates and accident alerts. This paper introduces $\pi$-ROAD, a framework designed to assist road emergency operators in managing network resources during incidents. By leveraging the vehicle's connectivity, $\pi$-ROAD constructs a road-specific network topology that allows operators to dynamically allocate bandwidth based on traffic density. The system's resource management capabilities are evaluated through a combination of simulation and real-world deployment. Results indicate that $\pi$-ROAD significantly enhances network performance during emergencies compared to existing solutions, offering a more efficient method for resource handling.

This study investigates the challenges of collaborative robotic navigation within dynamic, unstructured settings. It examines the application of the Artificial Potential Fields (APF) collision avoidance algorithm to enable two robots to transport a single object simultaneously. The research demonstrates that employing APF causes the robot to follow a suboptimal trajectory due to collision prevention maneuvers. To address this, the paper introduces a method to compute an optimal trajectory for the transporting task and integrates this with the APF algorithm to enhance the efficiency of the transportation process. The efficacy of the proposed approach is validated through both computer simulations and physical experiments.

The trajectory of urban development is increasingly defined by autonomous vehicles and machine intelligence. As these autonomous systems become more prevalent, they will reshape the physical fabric of the city, alter human behaviors, and redefine social interactions. This article examines the transformative impacts of autonomous transportation on urban environments and explores potential future trajectories.

This study investigates online caching with side information, where the adversary possesses an oracle capable of predicting the requested item for any time slot. We introduce a novel online algorithm that integrates cache management with a nearest neighbor recommendation system. We demonstrate that the competitive ratio improves as prediction accuracy increases and as the cache size grows. Specifically, the proposed algorithm achieves a competitive advantage of $1+\epsilon$ when the prediction error is bounded by $\epsilon \cdot \log m$, where $m$ represents the total number of items. Furthermore, we establish that the competitive ratio is monotonically increasing with respect to cache size. We also analyze the scenario where the adversary has access to the algorithm's internal state, proving that the proposed method remains effective against such adaptive strategies.

We introduce the Trilateral Attention Network (TrANet), a new architecture designed for image segmentation that integrates three complementary pathways: a coarse-to-fine pathway, a skip-connection pathway, and a skip-connection pathway with feature fusion. The coarse-to-fine pathway leverages multi-scale context to enhance segmentation accuracy, while the skip-connection pathway refines spatial details by passing features directly from early to late stages. The skip-connection pathway with feature fusion further optimizes performance by fusing intermediate features to capture multi-level representations. Extensive experiments on three prominent datasets—Pascal VOC 2012, Cityscapes, and ADE20K—demonstrate that TrANet achieves state-of-the-art results across all benchmarks. The source code is publicly available at https://github.com/yzh1995/TrANet.

We examine the geometry of $\mathcal{N}=1$ supersymmetric $d=4$ superconformal supergravity by analyzing the constraints imposed on torsion and curvature within the spinor superspace framework. Our findings demonstrate that, under the standard assumption that torsion constraints apply to gauge fields of linearized supergeometry only, the resulting system corresponds to the first-order torsion constraints of flat Minkowski space. Furthermore, we establish that the torsion constraints on torsion are sufficient to determine the strength of the curvature field's strength in the context of supergravity.

The efficacy of a learning model is heavily dependent on the quality of its training data. While recent research has focused on identifying and removing low-quality examples, our work instead examines how their individual contributions to a model can reveal insights into data quality. We introduce a novel approach that utilizes the model's output gradients to quantify the influence of each training instance. Our findings demonstrate that this gradient-based metric effectively identifies key components of the training set, including those that are most critical, those that are redundant, and instances that violate label consistency. Furthermore, our analysis indicates that this method remains robust across various model architectures and is applicable to a wide range of machine learning tasks.

We investigate the quantum charge pumping mechanism within the surface of a quantum anomalous Hall insulator, which is driven by non-linear optical effects. Our analysis reveals that the non-abelian matrix Berry phase, which is associated with spin-valley degrees of freedom in the two-dimensional topological insulator's surface, serves as a critical driver for this pumping phenomenon. Furthermore, we establish that the resulting spin-valley-resolved quantum charge pumping coefficient, which is defined by the surface Hall conductivity, scales quadratically with frequency.

We introduce METRO-LM, a series of Transformer language models ranging from 100M to 1B parameters, trained on a curated dataset of 300 GB from the Common Crawl. These models are optimized for efficiency and trained on a massive scale using a distributed infrastructure that supports petabytes of data and thousands of GPUs. Despite their high capacity, METRO-LM models significantly outperform earlier, smaller counterparts on various benchmarks, including MMLU, GSM8K, and HumanEval. Furthermore, we demonstrate that the training and inference performance of our models can be further enhanced by applying specific techniques.

We introduce a protocol for inferring the topology of quantum networks composed of interconnected quantum memories, relying exclusively on local measurements taken at individual nodes. This approach is applicable to diverse systems, including those utilizing photonic links and those employing quantum teleportation. Furthermore, we demonstrate that the network's topological structure can be recovered from measurements taken on a single memory, even when the network's size is exponentially large.

This research investigates how to present visualizations to users unfamiliar with their design. We examined three approaches: textual, visual, and combined (textual and visual) introductions. A user study involving 100 participants analyzed a visual encod ing displaying the top 100 most-cited papers in computer science, with introductions varying by these three methods. The study measured success through comprehension, information recall, and the ability to identify the visualization's key insight. The findings indicate that visual introductions are the most effective strategy, outperforming both text-based and combined approaches.

Floquet heating poses a significant challenge in the optical control of quantum many-body systems. This study examines the time evolution of a quantum spin chain subjected to a non-integrable, time-dependent Hamiltonian. We demonstrate that the Floquet heating mechanism can be mitigated by adjusting the driving amplitude, thereby extending the lifetime of specific quantum orders. Furthermore, we elucidate the connection between this phenomenon and the non-local characteristics of the Floquet Hamiltonian.

Counterfactual reasoning generates plans by exploring hypothetical scenarios, yet these plans often fail when executed due to inaccuracies in model parameters. This paper introduces a new method for deriving counterfactuals that explicitly incorporates uncertainty regarding such parameters. We frame the problem as a two-player game between a planner and an adversary who selects a parameter value to undermine the plan's effectiveness. We demonstrate that the best-response strategy for the adversary can be computed using Mixed Integer Linear Programming (MILP), while the planner's optimal strategy is formulated as a Bayesian Stackelberg game. We evaluate our approach against a standard method that ignores parameter uncertainty, using a scenario where an adversary chooses a parameter value after observing the planner's strategy. Results indicate that plans developed without accounting for uncertainty are frequently rendered ineffective by minor uncertainties, whereas our uncertainty-aware plans demonstrate greater robustness.

The collection comprises 1,000 audio files sourced from 200 distinct locations across 20 cities in the United States and the United Kingdom. This paper introduces Cain, a compiler designed for the SCAMP-5 language that generates code comparable to that of other systems. The assembly output produced by Cain is consistently shorter than that of SCAMP-5. Our implementation leverages LLVM infrastructure, utilizing its instruction set and library for assembly generation. The compiler's architecture is divided into three primary phases: SCAMP-5 to LLVM IR conversion, the LLVM IR code generation process, and final assembly. Within each SCAMP-5 to LLVM IR conversion phase, the compiler is further structured into two distinct components: an SCAMP-5 to LLVM IR code generator and a SCAMP-5 to LLVM IR disassembler.

We investigate the generalized Witten effect within the framework of quantum gravity, demonstrating that it imposes spectrum bounds on charged states. Leveraging this constraint, we narrow the search range for candidate microscopic states responsible for black hole entropy. Furthermore, we demonstrate that this effect eliminates specific theories from consideration, notably those exhibiting massless charged particles.

We introduce three enhancements to the regret pruning technique, which is designed to approximate Nash equilibria in extensive games with perfect information. The first enhancement involves two newly created pruning variations that are more effective than the original variant. The second enhancement addresses the issue of underestimating the regret threshold. The third enhancement employs a more precise method for calculating estimated regrets. We demonstrate that these three improvements are compatible with one another. The experiments indicate that these new methods yield substantial performance gains over both the unmodified regret pruning approach and the recently proposed Monte Carlo-based regret pruning algorithm.

This paper presents a novel modal logic grounded in possible states-of-affairs, which we utilize to reconstruct Aristotle's modal syllogistic. Our approach offers a fresh perspective by treating modal propositions as relations between particular states-of-affairs and worlds, thereby enabling a more straightforward demonstration of Aristotle's proofs through the elimination of fallacies in his reasoning. Furthermore, this framework clarifies the origins of these fallacies by revealing how they stem from invalid inferences that arise when treating modal propositions as if they were simple categorical propositions.

The detection efficiency threshold necessary to breach causal inequalities is significantly lower than that required for violating entanglement-based inequalities. This paper investigates classical causal inequalities within frameworks of general quantum causal models, demonstrating that violating these inequalities demands a lower detection efficiency than traditional quantum inequalities. Furthermore, we examine a specific class of classical causal models, proving that in these instances, violating a classical causal structure inevitably implies the violation of entanglement.

This study introduces a dual-critic reinforcement learning framework designed to manage video encoding by simultaneously optimizing rate-distortion performance and temporal consistency. By employing two independent critics to assess the value of state pairs under distinct reward functions, the proposed method effectively manages the conflicting requirements of minimizing distortion and adhering to rate constraints. The findings demonstrate that this framework achieves superior rate-distortion efficiency compared to standard RL-based encoders and maintains robust performance across a wide spectrum of rate limits, unlike prior RL approaches that often fail to handle rate constraints adequately.

This study investigates the impact of grain photo-ablation on the gas-phase chemistry within protoplanetary disks. We introduce a new chemical model that accounts for the photodestruction of carbon-rich grains, specifically graphite and amorphous carbon, alongside the destruction of silicate grains. This process is driven by the Lyman continuum and soft X-ray radiation from the central star. Our findings indicate that the resulting ablation of carbon-rich grains establishes a long-lived equilibrium cycle in the disk's gas-phase chemistry. This cycle involves the photodestruction of carbon grains releasing carbon atoms, which then form carbon monoxide (CO) and subsequently carbon monoxide ions (CO$^+$) via ionization. These ions subsequently recombine to form graphite grains, which are subsequently destroyed by further photodestruction. This cycle is most significant in disks with carbon-rich grains and low X-ray luminosity. Additionally, the process is most impactful in the disk's surface layers, where the intensity of the Lyman continuum radiation is highest.

This paper introduces NeuralCut, a new approach for selecting cuts in mixed-integer linear programming (MILP) that leverages neural networks. By training on extensive datasets of past solver states and the cuts they generated, NeuralCut learns to predict the most beneficial cuts for future states. Our experiments show that this method significantly outperforms existing baselines, including greedy selection, random sampling, and current state-of-the-art reinforcement learning models. Our findings indicate that NeuralCut can substantially reduce solver runtime, cutting the average time to solve a set of benchmark instances by 15%.

The superconducting behavior of the topological insulator T$_d$-MoTe$_2$ has been significantly altered by the substitution of Mo with Ir. This study examines the superconducting properties of T$_d$-Mo$_{1-x}$Ir$_{1-x}$Te$_2$ across varying Ir concentrations, revealing that the superconducting critical temperature ($T_c$) follows a non-monotonic trend with increasing Ir content. Specifically, $T_c$ rises from 0.35 K at $x=0$ to a peak of 0.62 K at $x=0.05$, before declining to 0.23 K at $x=0.10$. Analysis of the temperature dependence of the superconducting critical field $H_{c2}(T)$ indicates that the material exhibits s-wave superconductivity. Furthermore, the superconducting gap $\Delta$ was determined to be 0.30 ± 0.05 mV at $T=0$ K, yielding a 2$\Delta$/ $k_B T_c$ ratio of 2.9 ± 0.5. These findings suggest the material displays weak-coupling superconductivity.

Duplicate bug reports are a prevalent and costly issue within software development. While traditional methods rely on keyword matching to identify exact duplicates, this approach often fails to capture subtle semantic differences. To address this, we propose a novel strategy that leverages Natural Language Processing (NLP) to retrieve identical bug reports. Our approach involves training a transformer-based model to generate fixed-length embeddings for bug reports, which are subsequently stored in a vector database. We evaluate our method against the industry-standard tool, the ElasticSearch engine, using the industry-standard GitHub dataset. Our results demonstrate that our NLP-driven method significantly surpasses keyword matching and achieves performance comparable to the state-of-the-art tool.

We introduce an effective field theory framework that captures the essential physics of the phase transitions occurring in graphene subjected to strain. This model, characterized by strong coupling, utilizes a complex order parameter to describe the resulting phases. By employing the $1/N$ expansion, we establish the theory's foundational elements and derive the corresponding gap equations. Our analysis reveals that the transition from the pristine to the strained graphene ground state is second-order. Furthermore, we identify the existence of a distinct phase that emerges at a specific critical strain value, characterized by a non-zero order parameter.

This paper introduces a self-training framework for Named Entity Recognition (NER) that leverages the teacher-student paradigm to enhance model performance. The proposed method utilizes a teacher model to generate pseudo-labels for unlabeled data, which are subsequently used to train a student model. The study evaluates this framework across various scenarios, including single and multi-task learning environments, as well as transfer learning scenarios. The results indicate that the approach effectively improves NER outcomes, particularly when the student model is trained on limited labeled data.

The travel and hospitality sector is a massive global industry that relies heavily on consumer reviews and social media interactions to understand visitor needs and preferences. This study introduces a new approach for analyzing tourism-related discussions on social platforms, utilizing a dataset comprising 1.5 million tweets tagged with the #travel tag. By applying Natural Language Processing (NLP) techniques, we identify key topics within these tweets, which are then mapped onto the elements of the "travel experience" framework. Our analysis reveals that the content of these tweets is closely tied to specific components of that travel experience model. Furthermore, we examine the relationship between these tweets and the types of accounts that post them, demonstrating that different user categories exhibit distinct tweet contents. These findings offer valuable insights for businesses seeking to enhance their services and customer experiences.

This study introduces a machine learning framework for predicting the effective properties of microstructured materials, specifically focusing on the homogenization of the elastic behavior of linear, isotropic, and periodic composites. The approach utilizes the U-Net architecture, a convolutional neural network designed for image processing, to solve the linear elasticity equations governing this problem. The model is trained using the finite element method (FEM) to generate a dataset of periodic microstructures alongside their corresponding effective properties. The results demonstrate that the proposed ML framework achieves high accuracy in predicting effective properties for unseen microstructures, with the U-Net architecture successfully capturing the necessary spatial details of the periodic patterns.

We report the detection of a companion to the young star CI Tau at a separation of 0.14 arcseconds (equivalent to 10 au) using the Gemini Planet Imager. This companion, identified as CI Tau b, has a mass of 1.5 Jupiter masses and a projected orbital distance of 10 au. We have tracked its position over a period of 1.5 years, observing a change in its projected separation of 0.02 arcseconds (or 1.4 au). This orbital motion is consistent with a circular orbit, a scenario supported by the companion's low mass and spectral type of M6.5. We have ruled out alternative explanations for the observed motion, such as the "wobble" caused by a third body, because the resulting angular differential imaging upper limits exceed the maximum possible signal from such a configuration. We also excluded the possibility that the motion is due to the companion's orbital precession, noting that the observed displacement is only 10% of the magnitude required to produce the observed effect. We introduce a framework to map the finite-energy free-motion trajectories on a sphere to zero-energy paths in a specific two-dimensional potential. This potential is constructed by deriving it from a Dirac equation involving a specific choice of boundary conditions. The study further demonstrates that the B\"acklund transformation for both finite-energy free spherical motions and zero-energy orbits at this potential can be derived from the aforementioned Dirac equation. Finally, we establish a correspondence between these orbits and the B\"acklund transformation for finite-energy geodesics.

This paper introduces a novel approach to multi-object filtering in the absence of labels, utilizing a Bayes filter to derive a solution from the Multiple Hypothesis Tracking (MHT) framework. This method is implemented within the Multiple Cardinality Consensus (MCC) algorithm, which is enhanced by a new consensus mechanism. This mechanism leverages the consensus matrix to generate a consensus tree, which is subsequently employed to expand the solution space for trajectory estimation. The proposed algorithm is evaluated against established methods using a standard synthetic dataset, with results demonstrating its effectiveness. Furthermore, the method is applied to a real-world scenario involving a quadcopter tracking multiple targets.

The surge in power systems featuring high converter penetration has necessitated a new stability evaluation framework. Unlike conventional methods that rely on linearizing the system around an operating point, this paper introduces a criterion based on the system's state trajectory. This approach is validated using a two-machine, infinite bus model, where the assessment of small-disturbance asymptotic stability is demonstrated to be equivalent to that of traditional methods. Furthermore, this novel criterion is applied to a 39-bus system to illustrate its practical utility.

Signature forgery detection is a vital challenge in document authentication, yet it remains under-researched due to the scarcity of annotated data. This study introduces a novel approach to enhance the performance of signature verification models for forgery detection by leveraging three specific template attributes: distinctiveness, complexity, and repetition. Distinctiveness and complexity are derived from the original signature, while repetition is established by creating multiple copies of the signature. This framework utilizes the similarity scores from signature verification models to train a binary classifier that distinguishes between genuine and forged forgeries. Experimental results indicate that incorporating these template attributes can significantly boost detection performance. Furthermore, the proposed method is adaptable to various signature verification models and remains effective even with limited training data.
This work establishes a correspondence between Hardy sums and oriented geodesics. Leveraging this approach, we demonstrate that Hardy sums can be expressed via generalized Hardy-Littlewood formulas.

Mobile applications have become a primary means of accessing the internet, yet they often fail to deliver personalized experiences. To address this, we introduce a new framework designed to deliver customized content within mobile apps. This approach leverages the persistent context of users—such as their location and time—to create personalized, contextual recommendations. By utilizing a hybrid model that integrates both collaborative filtering and item-based filtering, the system identifies and suggests personalized webpages. Furthermore, it employs a contextual-aware injection mechanism to seamlessly embed these recommendations into a webpage's DOM structure. We evaluated this framework using the Flipkart app, a leading Indian e-commerce platform, and tested it with a dataset comprising 100,000 user sessions. The results demonstrate that the proposed framework can effectively integrate personalized recommendations into mobile applications.

This study introduces a novel real-time 6DoF pose estimation architecture that leverages a multi-scale feature pyramid and a dual-branch network to enhance accuracy. The framework employs a multi-scale feature pyramid to extract hierarchical features from input images, while a dual-branch design processes these multi-scale representations to generate precise 6DoF outputs. The system's effectiveness is validated through real-time testing on the real-world dataset, achieving an average rotation error of 0.19° and a translation error of 0.03 m.

This study details the performance of the 120–500 keV X-ray spectrometer aboard India's AstroSat mission, focusing on the collimator's capabilities. The collimator, equipped with a 10° field of view, is designed to observe bright point sources and extended objects. We report on the collimator's performance, including its sensitivity and the reliability of flux measurements for specific celestial targets. While the instrument has detected several point sources, flux measurements remain reliable only for Sco X-1 and Cygnus X-1. Additionally, the collimator has successfully observed various extended objects, including the Galactic Center, the Large Magellanic Cloud, the Small Magellanic Cloud, and the Andromeda galaxy.

Blockchain protocols can be categorized based on their access control mechanisms as either permissioned or permissionless systems. In this study, we introduce a novel framework designed to analyze the impact of these mechanisms on the protocol's consensus performance. We demonstrate that while the consensus protocols of permissionless blockchains can be modeled as Markov chains, those of permissioned blockchains are better represented as semi-Markov chains. We apply this framework to examine the consensus protocols of permissionless blockchains, specifically analyzing their average consensus delay and variance. Furthermore, we utilize the semi-Markov model to derive the theoretical bounds regarding the average consensus delay for permissioned blockchains.

This study examines the mass spectra of the $X(3872)$ and $Z_c(3900)$ within the framework of the refined chromomagnetic interaction model. We demonstrate that, consistent with experimental findings, the $X(3872)$ is identified as the $^{3P_1}$ state of the $[du\bar{c}\bar{d}]$ configuration, while the $Z_c(3900)$ corresponds to the $^{3P_2}$ state of the $[cu\bar{d}\bar{u}]$ arrangement.

This study examines the stability scale within an extended Standard Model featuring a complex, singlet Higgs field. We derive and analyze the corresponding Higgs potential, accounting for corrections from both the new Higgs field and the existing Standard Model components. Our findings indicate that the Higgs mass upper bound is influenced by the scale of instability. Specifically, when the new Higgs mass is small, the bound on the Higgs mass remains largely unaffected.

This study demonstrates that the solution to the Hamilton-Jacobi equation within Carnot groups satisfies a specific inequality of type $p$ introduced by Carlier and Maas. Furthermore, we establish the necessity of a $p$-Gromov-Hausdorff condition, specifically the $p$-Talagrand inequality, as a fundamental prerequisite for such Carnot groups to possess a logarithmic Sobolev inequality.

Exponentially weighted divergence (EWD) estimators are a class of estimators that are asymptotically linked to density power divergence (DPD) estimators. This paper examines the asymptotic behavior of EWD estimators, demonstrating that they inherit the desirable robustness and computational efficiency of DPD estimators. We provide a comparative analysis of their performance using Monte Carlo simulations and real data applications. The results indicate that, in terms of performance, EWD estimators are comparable to DPD estimators and often superior, while maintaining the same level of robustness.

This study introduces a new method for segmenting motion in images, designed to identify and classify pixels as either static or motion-oriented. The approach begins by calculating the correlation between a pixel and its neighbors within a local window, followed by a Gaussian smoothing step to refine the correlation values. Subsequently, a thresholding mechanism is applied to isolate the motion-oriented pixels. The proposed algorithm is validated using the standard Brodatz texture collection, demonstrating that it outperforms existing methods in both accuracy and speed.

We examine the fluctuations of coefficients in the characteristic polynomials of specific directed graphs, including periodic maps and covers of compact Riemann surfaces. Our findings indicate that when periodic orbits exhibit self-intersections, these variations are governed by the spatio-temporal correlations between them. This relationship is quantified through the self-intersection formula of periodic maps. Consequently, for the Riemann zeta function, we derive an upper limit on the variance of coefficients that is only marginally higher than the predictions made by the Gaussian Unitary Ensemble.

Variable stars (VS) are a cornerstone of the Milky Way's stellar population, with the majority exhibiting periodic behaviors. This study introduces a new method for classifying periodic VS using the Gaia Data Release 3 (DR3) Exoplanet Host Characterization (EPIC) catalog. The proposed approach leverages the EPIC catalog's existing classification of periodic VS, which is derived from the photometric light curves of 1,000,000+ EPIC targets. The method involves cross-matching the EPIC catalog with Gaia DR3 to identify periodic VS, followed by a detailed analysis of their light curve properties. The results demonstrate that light curve characteristics can effectively distinguish between different periodic VS types. Specifically, eclipsing binaries display distinct features compared to other periodic variables, such as the nebular variables (NEB), which are characterized by irregular brightness fluctuations. Additionally, the study identifies that the periodicity of these VS is strongly correlated with their variability amplitude. This work addresses the characterization of the closest negative imaginary system to a given linear time invariant (LTI) non-negative imaginary one. By applying the nearest non-negative imaginary output projection technique, the solution is derived as a specific positive semi-definite projection of a specified matrix onto the manifold of non-negative imaginary systems. The paper also establishes the conditions necessary for uniqueness and provides illustrative examples to validate the theoretical findings.

Continual learning (CL) has recently emerged as a promising avenue for End-to-End Automatic Speech Recognition (EER), offering a way to sequentially train on new tasks without compromising prior knowledge. This paper investigates the application of CL to EER, specifically examining how it handles the learning of new languages and acoustic domains. We demonstrate that top-tier CL techniques can enhance performance on new tasks by up to 10% relative to standard fine-tuning, all while maintaining performance levels comparable to initial training from scratch. Furthermore, we show that these methods can be applied to pre-trained Whisper models to acquire new languages with a 20% relative improvement over fine-tuning. Finally, we introduce a data-efficient approach that leverages a single hour of data to achieve a 5% relative gain over fine-tuning for new whisper models.

Sentiment analysis is a vital component of social media analytics, yet it becomes significantly more difficult when users employ code-switching, a prevalent feature of social media communication. This phenomenon involves mixing words from different languages, such as writing English alongside Chinese characters. This paper introduces a novel approach to address code-switching sentiment analysis by utilizing pre-trained language models. Our methodology involves identifying code-switching segments and utilizing these segments to fine-tune pre-trained models. Our findings indicate that this strategy outperforms existing state-of-the-art methods, particularly in scenarios where code-switching exhibits high levels of complexity.

This study examines the three-loop seesaw model, which generates Majorana neutrino masses through two distinct three-loop diagrams. We analyze the resulting mass spectrum and determine the decay widths of the model's heavy leptons, finding that decay channels involving light neutrinos are significantly suppressed. Consequently, we identify that the model predicts a lightest heavy lepton with a mass below 129 GeV, rendering it accessible at the Large Hadron Collider. Furthermore, we demonstrate that this model can account for the observed baryon asymmetry of the universe via the mechanism of thermal leptogenesis.

Product-based Neural Networks (PNNs) are a type of deep learning architecture designed to handle categorical data, with a core structure that captures interactions between categories. While PNNs have been widely adopted in various applications, their training process is often hindered by the challenge of selecting appropriate network structures. This paper introduces a method for automatically determining the optimal PNN architecture, utilizing a black-box optimization framework to generate a decision tree that directly maps to network configurations. The approach is validated on two distinct datasets, demonstrating its ability to produce models that outperform those created using standard manual selection techniques.

This study investigates active reflecting surface (IRS)-assisted active transmitting beamforming to maximize the minimum achievable rate. The analysis accounts for channel uncertainty regarding both the links between users and the IRS, as well as the connections between the base station and the IRS. To address this, a robust optimization framework is developed, where the uncertainty models are integrated into the formulation. The resulting problem is non-convex and difficult to solve directly; therefore, a semi-definite relaxation (SDR) technique is employed to transform it into an equivalent robust semidefinite programming (RSDP) model. Furthermore, a low-complexity alternating optimization algorithm is proposed to iteratively update beamforming vectors and the optimal reflection coefficients of the IRS. Numerical simulations demonstrate that the suggested approach achieves significant performance gains compared to baseline schemes, while confirming that incorporating CSI uncertainty into the robust design is essential for optimal results.

Branch prediction is a pivotal component of modern computing, and conventional static predictors often fail to match the precision of emerging dynamic approaches. While dynamic methods can significantly enhance performance, their high overhead frequently hinders their adoption. This paper introduces a hybrid predictor leveraging deep learning, combining the efficiency of static techniques with the adaptive strength of dynamic ones. The system employs a dedicated deep learning model to forecast outcomes, utilizing the static predictor as a fallback when the dynamic prediction is deemed unreliable. Evaluation across the SPEC CPU2006 benchmark suite demonstrates that our approach achieves a 10.4% reduction in mispredictions compared to traditional branch prediction, yielding a 10.4% performance improvement.

This paper introduces a deep convolutional neural network designed to autonomously manage a camera's movements and tracking within a multi-view surveillance framework. This approach eliminates the need for manually designed, domain-specific features traditionally used for camera control and target monitoring, instead leveraging the network's ability to learn directly from raw image data. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed system outperforms existing state-of-the-art methods in both detection accuracy and computational efficiency.
We investigate the SOS model on a half-space under boundary conditions, demonstrating that the boundary laws for the model are not normalizable when applied to the model's non-flat settings.

This study introduces a new approach to characterize entangled two-photon resonance energy transfer (E2P) within a single-molecule framework. The proposed method utilizes the effective rate coefficient, $K_{E2P}$, to quantify this process. The authors demonstrate that the effective rate coefficient $K_{E2P}$ can be determined through a straightforward single-molecule spectroscopy technique involving excitation with two-pulse laser pulses. The relationship between $K_{E2P}$ and the transfer rate constant ($k_{E2P}$) is derived from the average number of E2P events per excitation cycle ($\bar{n}$), expressed as $K_{E2P} = k_{E2P}/\tau_{\rm rep}$, where $\tau_{\rm rep}$ represents the interval between excitation pulses. The paper further illustrates the application of this method by analyzing entangled E2P in the photosynthetic complex from *Rhodobacter sphaeroides* 2.4.1, specifically focusing on the transfer of energy from the accessory chlorophyll to the reaction center.

This study examines the strong coupling constants $\lambda_{\eta_{c}}$ and $\lambda_{\eta_{b}}$ for the respective pseudoscalar mesons using light-cone QCD sum rules. The results are derived by incorporating the full operator product expansion (OPE) spectrum within the QCD sum rules framework. Our findings demonstrate that the obtained strong coupling constants align well with predictions from both the non-relativistic quark model and potential models.

This paper demonstrates that the "implied weights" generated by linear regression techniques, such as propensity score weighting, can be utilized to construct an optimal observational study design. By framing these weights as treatment allocation strategies, researchers can evaluate and contrast multiple observations studies to identify the one that minimizes bias in causal estimation. The analysis further proves that, under a specific set of assumptions, the optimization problem for these weights is convex, enabling the application of efficient numerical methods to derive the ideal study design. Additionally, the approach is extended to scenarios involving multiple treatments and continuous treatment levels. Finally, the proposed methodology is validated through a simulation study and applied to observational data from a clinical trial investigating the efficacy of the antidiabetic drug pioglitazone.

Voltage Source Converters (VSCs) are increasingly utilized to connect renewable energy sources to the grid. In this context, VSCs are capable of damping oscillations and enhancing grid resilience through active control mechanisms. This paper investigates the impact of a VSC on a weakly coupled grid, focusing on the interaction between the converter and the network. The study employs a linearized model of the VSC, which incorporates control dynamics, a three-phase bridge, and an output filter. To evaluate the system's behavior, a comprehensive sensitivity analysis is conducted, examining how specific parameters influence the dynamics of the VSC-network pair. The investigation covers both the effects of varying individual parameters and the influence of different control strategies on the network's dynamic response.

We introduce a theoretical framework for analyzing the quantum dynamics of a large atomic ensemble, accounting for both collective and individual atomic behaviors. This model utilizes a two-body interaction term to represent the influence of a specific atom on the rest of the group. Applying this approach, we examine the quantum evolution of two atoms within the larger ensemble, observing that emitted light displays sub-Poissonian photon statistics. Furthermore, we analyze the scenario where one atom is excited to the upper level and the other to the lower level; in this state, the population difference decays via a non-exponential process, resulting in emitted radiation with bunched (super-sub-Poissonian) photon statistics.

This study examines the stability of kink solutions within nonlinear systems featuring internal modes. We establish that internal dynamics significantly influence kink stability, enabling both stable and unstable configurations. Furthermore, we demonstrate that the internal mode's contribution to kcent stability can be precisely modeled using a double-well potential.

Generalized parton distributions (GPDs) are essential for understanding high-energy hadron interactions and the kinematics of exclusive and inclusive hadron production. This study examines the impact of the dynamical dressing of quark-gluon fields on quark GPDs, utilizing a dynamical model derived from quantum chromodynamics (QCD) that incorporates a running coupling. The analysis focuses on the impact factor for the $q+g \to q+g$ Compton scattering process, which is critical for high-energy photon-hadron interactions. Results indicate that accounting for the dynamical dressing of the quark field significantly modifies the impact factor, specifically affecting the soft-gluon region. This finding suggests that hadronization can be described as a two-step mechanism: first, the quark radiates a soft gluon, and subsequently, the quark-gluon pair transitions into a jet.

Text classification is a prevalent natural language processing task, yet it is vulnerable to adversarial attacks that alter input words minimally to force incorrect predictions. This study introduces a novel defense strategy by integrating discrete noise into the training data, which effectively shifts the model's decision boundary to its advantage. We demonstrate that this noise acts as a potent barrier against adversarial examples, while remaining imperceptible to human readers. Our proposed method, termed Adversarial Noise (AN), was evaluated across four datasets using three distinct classifiers. Results indicate that AN achieves a significant reduction in adversarial accuracy loss compared to existing defenses, while maintaining high accuracy on clean data.

Accurate polyp detection is essential for endoscopic procedures, yet the small size of these polyps and the challenges posed by the endoscope's motion blur complicate detection. This paper introduces a new channel-aware attention mechanism designed to enhance feature aggregation for polyp detection. By leveraging the distinct spatial-temporal characteristics of polyp detection, the proposed channel-aware attention module aggregates features across both channels and time, thereby improving the network's ability to capture relevant information. Furthermore, the method employs a multi-scale feature fusion strategy to address variations in polyp size. Experimental results on the MS-Polyp and IRRM-Datasets demonstrate that our approach outperforms existing state-of-the-art methods.

The rp-process is a rapid proton-capture sequence occurring in Type-I X-ray bursts, where the reaction flow is governed by the interplay between nuclear reaction rates and Coulomb barriers. This study examines the impact of Coulomb barrier penetration on the rp-process during a Type-I X-ray burst simulation. We employed a Monte Carlo method to calculate the time-dependent evolution of the reaction network, incorporating both direct and resonant Coulomb barrier penetrations for all relevant reactions. Our results indicate that approximately 10% of the process flow bypasses the waiting point $^{56}$Ni, and roughly 15% bypasses the waiting point $^{60}$Zn. Additionally, we calculated the energy generation rate and nucleosynthesis yields for a specific set of initial conditions.

In this work, we examine the structure of the special fiber of an abelian scheme's morphism to its base, specifically the map restricted to the kernel of reduction modulo $\mathfrak{p}$. We demonstrate that the irreducible components forming the flat section of this kernel can be characterized as torsor cosets. Furthermore, we establish that the generic point of any such torse coset corresponds to a point in the generic fiber of the special fiber's flat part, and conversely, every generic point of the flat section arises from a unique torsor coset. Additionally, we investigate the geometric implications of this duality and provide an explicit description of the unipotent radical of the special fiber's unipotent reduction.

The Fermi-LAT mission has significantly advanced our understanding of the diffuse Galactic gamma-ray emission, yet it has struggled to detect point sources above the Very High Energy (VHE) threshold. Consequently, Very High Energy gamma-ray observations have become essential for clarifying the origins of emission in the GeV range. This review outlines the current state of VHE astronomy, focusing on recent findings from the H.E.S.S. observatory.

This study examines the geometric singularities of a diffusion process within a bounded domain $\Omega \subset \mathbb{R}^n$, subject to nonlocal boundary constraints. Specifically, the flux across the boundary $\partial\Omega$ is governed by an integral operator acting on the entire boundary. The primary objective is to establish precise regularity criteria for solutions to this boundary value problem. The analysis demonstrates that while regularity in the interior holds for any $u \in C^{1,1}(\Omega)$, the behavior near the boundary is contingent upon the geometric properties of $\partial\Omega$. In the case where $\partial\Omega$ is sufficiently smooth, the solution exhibits Hölder continuity. Conversely, if the boundary is merely Lipschitz continuous, the solution attains Hölder continuity within the domain $\Omega$.

We have created a dataset comprising 1,000 compact stellar systems (CSSs), each with 100 artificial colors, by simulating the superposition of a stellar population and a point source. These point sources represent either an A0V star or a quiescent AGN, with magnitudes varying from 0 to 10. Our analysis indicates that CSS colors remain largely unaffected by the point source, whereas their colors shift significantly. Consequently, we applied a convolutional neural network (CNN) to classify these objects into CSS or point source categories. Furthermore, we utilized the CNN to distinguish between A0V stars and AGNs. Our results demonstrate that the CNN achieves a classification accuracy of 99.9% for identifying CSSs and 98.9% for differentiating A0V stars from AGNs. Additionally, we determined that the blue, green, and red filters provide the most informative data for CSS classification, while the blue and green filters are most effective for distinguishing A0V stars from AGNs.

Simulations are frequently employed to model recommender systems, offering a controlled environment for refining and assessing their behavior. This paper examines the simulation of recommender systems, specifically addressing how it can streamline the development process and enhance the evaluation of outcomes.

This work introduces a hypothesis testing framework grounded in truncated sample means, designed for scenarios involving distributions with infinite mean or variance. By leveraging the convergence of truncated sample means to their population counterparts, we establish the consistency of tests based on distance metrics—such as the $L_2$ norm, Wasserstein distance, and Kolmogorov distance—when evaluated against these truncated populations. Furthermore, we demonstrate that under heavy-tailed conditions, where the $p$-th moment exists for $p < 2$, our proposed tests achieve asymptotic normality.

Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) have demonstrated significant potential in developing Brain-Computer Interfaces (BCIs) for signal processing and classification. However, CNNs suffer from two primary drawbacks: they are highly sensitive to noise and require extensive amounts of labeled data. This study addresses these limitations by integrating a denoising autoencoder (DAE) with CNNs. The proposed architecture first utilizes the DAE to preprocess EEG signals, thereby mitigating noise interference. Subsequently, the refined signals are fed into the CNN to extract features for classification. Experimental results indicate that this combined approach outperforms standalone CNNs in both accuracy and robustness against noise.

This study investigates the $AdS$ duality between a massive scalar field and a bulk scalar within a noncommutative framework. By employing a double holographic setup, we derive a bulk scalar potential that accounts for the noncommutative characteristics of the boundary theory. Furthermore, we demonstrate that the $AdS$ duality serves as a holographic representation of the noncommutative deformation applied to the massless scalar potential on the boundary.

This study examines the impact of incorporating incompatibility as a state variable within a Markov Decision Process (MDD) model designed for kidney transplantation. The primary objective is to determine if this enhancement allows for a more nuanced analysis of the acceptance decisions facing both patients and potential donors.

This study investigates the latent state organization of both Hidden Markov Models (HMMs) and Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks, contrasting them with Elman models. We demonstrate that HMMs and LSTMs maintain comparable structures in their latent states, whereas the organization of Elman latent states is markedly distinct. Furthermore, we show that the HMM's constructed state space aligns closely with the latent state organization found in LSTMs.

This work examines weighted Bergman spaces defined on the unit disc and investigates specific classes of compact operators belonging to the Schatten class within these spaces. We provide characterizations for symbols of functions in $H^\infty$ that ensure their associated multiplication operators fall into the Schatten class for such spaces.

We report the discovery of three new magnetic hot subdwarfs, designated as LHS 2886, LHS 2887, and LHS 2888, within the LAMOST survey. These objects were identified through their distinctive narrow, broadened, and shifted Balmer lines, which are characteristic of magnetic hot subdwarfs. Spectroscopic analysis of these stars reveals hydrogen abundances that are approximately 0.2 dex lower than current theoretical models predict. This discrepancy suggests that the stars possess a significant amount of helium in their outer layers, a feature likely caused by the diffusion of helium from their cores.

This study introduces a methodology for examining and reducing approximation errors in matrices by leveraging invariant factor and polynomial matrix theory. The approach involves converting the error analysis into a divisibility problem, which is then evaluated using the invariant factors of both the original matrix and the approximating matrix. Furthermore, we derive a novel expression for the distance between two matrices in terms of their invariant polynomials, an expression that is equivalent to the standard definition of matrix distance.

This study examines the distribution of hyperlinks within Wikipedia articles, analyzing both raw wikitext and rendered HTML to assess the impact of hyperlink syntax on word frequency. We demonstrate that the count of words associated with links varies significantly between these two formats, with wikitext exhibiting a distinct shift in distribution. Furthermore, we evaluate the lexical diversity of hyperlinked words across different language editions of Wikipedia.

The interplay between twisted bilayers and their interfacial polar domains offers a promising route to investigate topological physics. In this study, we demonstrate that the polar domains within twisted bilayer graphene (TBG) can be effectively described by an effective model featuring a tunable, twist-angle-dependent Berry phase. This phase significantly influences the system's electronic properties, including the emergence of Dirac cones, the presence of Dirac points, and the opening of band gaps. Our analysis reveals that the twist-angle-dependent Berry phase can be understood as a continuous transition between two distinct twisted bilayer configurations: one with a $C_2$ rotation symmetry and another with $C_4$ symmetry. This connection allows the model to be derived from the established continuum model of single-layer twisted bilayer graphene. Furthermore, we examine the impact of the Berry phase on the system's electronic properties, specifically its Chern number and Hall conductivity. Our findings indicate that the resulting Chern number is an integer, suggesting the potential presence of chiral edge states.

This study examines how light travels in a static, spherically symmetric universe with arbitrary spatial curvature. We derive the general equations for light propagation and demonstrate that, in a universe with non-flat geometry, a light ray's path deviates from a simple planar curve. Furthermore, we analyze how light rays behave as spherical spirals by calculating the spiral's pitch.

We investigate the behavior of a single colloid suspended in a liquid crystal within a two-dimensional wavy channel. This channel features an arrangement of alternating hills and valleys, where the liquid crystal's director field is aligned parallel to the wavy surface. We analyze the colloid's movement under the influence of an applied electric field, focusing on how the resulting trajectories vary with specific parameters. Our findings indicate that the flow patterns are highly sensitive to the alignment of the colloid's electrophoretic mobility and the magnitude of the applied electric field. Furthermore, we observe that the colloid's path is significantly impacted by the geometric curvature of the wall, the spacing between hills and valleys, and the specific boundary conditions governing the liquid crystal's director orientation.

The Roche limit defines the distance within which a celestial body's self-gravity cannot counteract tidal forces from a larger planet. When an asteroid approaches this limit, its elongation increases, signaling a heightened susceptibility to tidal disruption. This study examines the Roche limit of the main-belt asteroid (10199) Pythia, which has a diameter of approximately 10 km and a density of 2.5 g/cc. By analyzing the asteroid's elongation during its 2010 close approach to Jupiter, the Roche limit was determined to be $1.9 \pm 0.1$ Jupiter radii. This value aligns with theoretical predictions for a body with similar density and a shape factor of 0.33, assuming a strength of $10^4$ Pa. Furthermore, the observed elongation was compared with that of (10195) Bennu, a 500-meter-diameter asteroid that passed within 2.2 Jupiter radii of Jupiter in 2011. The comparison revealed that Pythia's elongation was significantly lower than Bennu's, suggesting that Pythia possesses a much higher structural strength.

Machine learning (ML) and quantum computing (QC) are increasingly vital for addressing complex scientific challenges. This study introduces a hybrid quantum-classical framework designed to analyze rare conformational transitions in molecular dynamics simulations. The approach employs ML techniques to identify and cluster distinct molecular conformations, which are then mapped onto a low-dimensional landscape. This reduced landscape is quantized using a quantum algorithm to calculate transition probabilities between states. We applied this methodology to the isomerization of a tris-peptide system, demonstrating that our method effectively captures rare events and accurately reproduces established kinetic models. Furthermore, we show that the proposed quantum algorithm can be executed on current quantum hardware, including noisy intermediate-scale quantum (NISQ) processors.

The MAPPIES code, a newly developed Monte-Carlo tool, enables the investigation of X-ray and gamma-ray polarisation through Compton scattering. It simulates the scattering of photons originating from a source with defined polarisation properties against an electron distribution, producing both polarised and unpolarised signals. This output can subsequently be processed to mimic experimental data. Furthermore, the software offers the capability to reverse this process: given a measured polarisation, it can deduce the likely characteristics of the electron distribution.

This study examines the seasonal development of categories for sea-ice thickness in the Laptev and East Siberian seas, utilizing a model derived from a nonlinear, time-dependent shallow-ice approximation. The framework incorporates a time-variable albedo that responds to the average thickness of the ice. The analysis focuses on the emergence of open water, specifically investigating how the timing and location of its appearance influence the resulting ice categories. The findings indicate that the category of maximum seasonal thickness is contingent upon the specific moment in the season when open water first appears. Furthermore, the category for minimum seasonal thickness is determined by the location of open water at the end of the season. The research concludes that the proposed model is capable of reproducing the observed seasonal evolution of sea-ice thickness categories.

Furthermore, we demonstrate that the curves $\mathcal X_{a,b,n}$ and $\mathcal Y_{n,s}$ constitute the sole instances of such coverings derived from Hermitian curves.

This study introduces NIPS4Bplus, an advanced version of the NIPS4B acoustic bird detection system, engineered to identify bird songs from the NIBS dataset. By leveraging a multi-task learning framework, NIPS4Bplus simultaneously classifies audio into ecoacoustic categories and detects bird species. We demonstrate the utility of NIPS4Bplus in ecological acoustic monitoring, specifically for tracking avian populations within forest ecosystems. The model's efficacy was assessed using a 10-fold cross-validation strategy, with performance evaluated through the F1 score.

Event cameras are increasingly utilized for vision tasks, particularly in scenarios demanding high temporal resolution. However, their calibration remains a challenging and underexplored area. This paper introduces a robust framework for calibrating event cameras that functions effectively with both static and dynamic scenes, eliminating the need for specific patterns or texture. The approach first computes the rotation and translation parameters by leveraging the correspondence between features in a frame-based camera and a synchronized event camera. Subsequently, it refines the intrinisic parameters of the event camera. This method can also perform extrinsic calibration between a frame-based system and a frame-based system. The framework is validated using both simulated data and real-world datasets.

Graph learning has proven effective in numerous domains, including social networking, e-commerce, knowledge graphs, and biological networks. However, existing research has predominantly focused on social and e-commerce networks, leaving the specific utility of graph learning for other fields largely unexplored. This study introduces a novel graph learning framework designed to model the complex, multi-relational interactions within knowledge graphs. By leveraging this framework, we successfully predict the relationships between entities and construct knowledge graphs from raw data. Furthermore, we demonstrate the practical value of this approach by building knowledge graphs for the Chinese film industry and the field of astronomy.

The action of the four-strand braid group on exceptional collections within the homological projective geometry of $\mathbb{F}_2$ Hirzebruch surfaces is analyzed, with specific attention given to identifying when these collections remain exceptional.

This study introduces a 3D guidance system for retinal surgery that utilizes a projector to overlay a virtual coordinate frame onto the patient's eye surface. By leveraging the projector's inherent 3D visualization capabilities, this method enhances the localization of the scleral needle, thereby improving the precision of the procedure. The proposed system comprises three primary components: a projector, a needle equipped with a magnetic marker, and a camera. The projector illuminates the eye surface with a distinct "spotlight" pattern, while the camera captures these projections from a distinct viewpoint to establish a unique mapping relationship. The system employs a virtual coordinate frame to track the eye surface, subsequently calculating the 3D coordinates of the needle relative to this frame. The accuracy of this approach was validated through in-vivo experiments involving a macula surgery simulation, demonstrating the system's effectiveness and precision.

We establish that the $F$-polynomial associated with any cluster algebra can be expressed as a product formula, which we subsequently expand into a product of sums. Leveraging this expansion, we demonstrate that for any given cluster algebra, there exists a cluster variable that serves as a lower bound for every $F$-polynomial.

The FIDO2 standard, which is gaining significant traction, is a crucial step in advancing the field of passwordless authentication. This research investigates how to integrate FIDO2 with the existing OpenStack authentication framework. We introduce an OpenStack extension that leverages FIDO2 to enable passwordless user authentication. This extension operates within the Keystone service by utilizing the FIDO2 Keyston service provider. We have developed this prototype in an effort to further the development of both the FIDO2 and OpenStack ecosystems.

This paper examines the expressive power of the $\pi$-calculus when compared to reactive Turing machines. We demonstrate that there exists a specific behavior, executable only by a finitely interactive device, which the $\pi$-calculus cannot specify. This uncomputability persists even within an expanded version of the $\pi$-calculus that permits infinite sums of prefix-pi terms. This result stands in contrast to previous findings by Boudol and Melliès, who showed that reactive Turing machines are less expressive than the $\pi$-calculus regarding behaviors with finite expressibility. This discrepancy highlights a key distinction between reactive Turing machines and the $\pi$-calculus: whereas the latter can describe behaviors that cannot be finitely executed, this property is not shared by reactive Turing machines.

This research introduces a designed Gray code for ordered trees, built upon the depth-first search method to navigate from one tree to the next within a defined search space. Furthermore, we provide a detailed analysis of the code's time complexity.

Reconstructing particle trajectories in heavy ion collisions is a complex task due to the high density of charged particles and the presence of overlapping events. This study introduces a new reconstruction algorithm utilizing a deep neural network (DNN) to enhance the efficiency of the track-finding process. The proposed method is benchmarked against the standard track reconstruction approach used in the CMS heavy ion analysis.

The time-discontinuous prismatic space-time (D-PST) approach is a novel technique designed to overcome the numerical instabilities and precision issues inherent in standard space-time (ST) finite elements when applied to free-surface flow simulations. The D-PST method extends the concept of discontinuous space-time (D-T) finite elements to three dimensions, offering superior accuracy and stability compared to traditional ST methods. By maintaining a fixed, explicit treatment of the free surface, the D-PST framework effectively circumvents the difficulties associated with the thin-layer ST method, such as the need for extremely fine element sizes and the challenge of preserving mass conservation. The proposed approach is validated through a series of numerical experiments involving two-dimensional and three-dimensional gravity waves, demonstrating its capability to accurately capture wave propagation and dispersion.

A circular $r_{_k}$-flow in a signed graph $G$ is defined as a circular $r_{_k}$-flow on the underlying undirected graph $U(G)$ that adheres to the sign constraints of $G$. In this work, we demonstrate that the presence of such a flow on $G$ is equivalent to the existence of a modulo $k$-orientation on $G$ where every odd face is properly oriented. Furthermore, we establish that a signed graph $G$ admits a circular $r_{_k}$-flow if and only if its cycle space is not contained within the span of the cycle $C_{\lfloor k/2 \rfloor}$.

We present a deterministic algorithm for the Modular Subset Sum problem that runs in $O(\log^2 n)$ time, representing a significant enhancement over the prior $O(n \log^2 n)$-time approach by Bj\"orkelund, Dasgupta, and Tzamos (2018). This method builds on the seminal $O(n)$-time algorithm for integer Subset Sum introduced by Schmidt and Mischke (1969). Our solution leverages the Chinese Remainder Theorem alongside a novel application of a deterministic variant of the Babai, Coppersmith, and Shamir technique for identifying short vectors within a lattice.

This study investigates the variability of M-dwarf stars within the Kepler field, utilizing a sample of 1,000 objects selected from the Kepler Input Catalog (KIC) that exhibit significant flux variations. By analyzing the light curves of these stars, we identified 1,000 objects with flaring behavior, 1,000 with rotational variability, and 1,000 non-variables. We then examined the frequency of flaring across different spectral types, finding that flaring is more prevalent in earlier M-dwarfs compared to later ones. We further explored the characteristics of flaring versus non-flaring variable stars, discovering that flaring stars are generally brighter, have shorter rotation periods, and display a bimodal distribution of rotational velocities.
