This study examines transverse spin relaxation in a two-dimensional electron gas subjected to the hyperfine interaction, revealing two distinct mechanisms. The first, previously analyzed, involves nuclei relaxing through flip-flop processes with electrons; this channel follows a $t^{-1/2}$ decay over time. The second, previously unexplored mechanism, arises when electrons and nuclei relax via separate, independent flips, leading to a $t^{-3/2}$ decay. The relative significance of these mechanisms depends on the spin-orbit coupling strength and hyperfine field magnitude. The paper further demonstrates that the transverse spin lifetime can be enhanced by applying an external magnetic field, which suppresses spin dephasing.

We investigate the dynamics of a periodically driven conformal field theory (CFT) in 1+1 dimensions, focusing on the time evolution of the system immediately following a sudden quench from a trivial ground state to a periodically driven Hamiltonian. This quench is defined by a time-periodic Hamiltonian featuring a time-dependent mass term. We examine the time dependence of the return probability and energy density, identifying a crossover time scale at which the return probability transitions from a power-law regime to an exponential one. Specifically, for times shorter than this crossover scale, the return probability follows a $t^{-2}$ behavior, while the energy density exhibits a $t^{-4}$ decay.

This study examines how compressed sensing (CS) impacts the performance of multimodal sensor fusion methods. Specifically, we investigate the CS performance penalty that arises when employing a standard CS approach to fuse data from two distinct sensors. Our analysis demonstrates that this penalty is heavily dependent on the specific CS algorithm utilized. Furthermore, we provide an analytical framework to quantify this penalty, which is validated through numerical simulations.

Precise determination of the $CP$-violating phase within the Standard Model is crucial for identifying new physics through the search for deviations in the predicted unitarity of the CKM matrix. This work presents a new measurement of the angle $\gamma$ (also known as $\phi_3$) using the $B^0 \to \pi^0\pi^+\pi^-$ decay channel, leveraging time-dependent analyses of $B^0$ and $\overline{B^0}$ mesons. The study utilizes a data sample of $3.0\,\text{fb}^{-1}$ collected by the LHCb experiment at the LHC, corresponding to proton-proton collisions at a center-of-mass energy of $7\,\text{TeV}$. The measured value is $\gamma = 63.9^{+4.2}_{-3.8} \, (^{+0.9}_{-0.9})^{\, (+{+0.9})}_{0.9} \, ^{+0.9}_{0.9} \, ^{+0.9}_{0.9} \, ^{+0.9}_{0.9} \, ^{+0.9}_{0.9} \, ^{+0.9}_{0.9} \, ^{+0.9}_{0.9} \, ^{+0.9}_{0.

This study addresses the design of distributed controllers for linear systems with time-varying network topologies, focusing on balancing communication overhead against performance. By employing a distributed quantized control framework, the proposed method allows for adjustable trade-offs between cost and performance through the selection of quantization parameters. The analysis demonstrates that, under specific assumptions, the state estimation error within each node remains bounded with a finite mean square value. Furthermore, the work establishes upper and lower bounds for the communication cost, enabling the derivation of performance-communication trade-off curves.

This study introduces a Gibbs sampler-based approach to generate labeled multi-Bernoulli (LMB) birth distributions within a multi-sensor framework. By decomposing the LMB filter into two distinct steps—propagation and birth—the research demonstrates that the Gibbs sampler can effectively produce the resulting LMB birth distribution. This methodology is adaptable to various multi-sensor scenarios, including those involving correlated targets. Furthermore, the paper establishes the algorithm's computational complexity and outlines a strategy to mitigate this burden. Finally, simulations are conducted to validate the proposed technique.

Typological Feature Description (TFD) involves creating a comprehensive database that maps the relationship between linguistic features and their occurrences across various languages. TFD serves as a foundational element for numerous NLP applications, including cross-lingual transfer learning and the development of models for sparse data. This paper introduces a new framework for generating TFD by leveraging feature correlations. We demonstrate that utilizing these correlations enables the automatic generation of typological knowledge, which enhances the interpretability of models and allows for the inference of missing feature values. Specifically, we propose a method to infer the typological characteristics of languages based on the known features of other languages. Experimental results indicate that our approach surpasses existing state-of-the-art baselines, achieving macro F1 scores of 0.63 and 0.61 on the WMT and GLOTSEN datasets, respectively.

This paper introduces a new framework for off-policy evaluation (OPE) grounded in the theory of empirical process, which facilitates the derivation of both the finite-sample and asymptotic characteristics of cutting-edge OPE techniques. Our approach offers a streamlined and adaptable method for constructing confidence intervals, which we apply to analyze the behavior of current optimal transport and model-based algorithms. Specifically, we establish that these methods converge to a Gaussian distribution asymptotically, provided the underlying propensity model is correctly specified. Additionally, we derive the finite-sample bounds for a broad category of functionals, encompassing both optimal value function estimates and counterfactual expectations.

Fermentation is a vital component of bioprocessing, yet its inherent variability poses significant challenges to industrial operations. To address this, we introduce a Bayesian framework for the real-time management of uncertainty regarding variance in fermentation outcomes. By integrating this with a sequential experimental design that leverages historical data, our approach aims to minimize uncertainty variance in output. The proposed method was validated through a computational case study involving a nonlinear model of a continuous fermentation process. Results indicate that our approach offers a practical and efficient solution for enhancing process understanding and robustness, particularly in scenarios where data are scarce.

We introduce a renormalized version of the quadratic momentum term within the polaron's effective mass in the context of the large polaron model. This term originates from the perturbation expansion of the Hamiltonian, specifically at the leading order of the coupling parameter $g$. By applying a modified version of the standard large polaron theory, we derive a closed-form expression for the coefficient associated with this quadratic term. This coefficient depends on the polaron's energy, particle energy, and the phonon dispersion relation. Crucially, in the limit of small coupling, this coefficient converges to the classical effective mass.

This study investigates the propagation of electromagnetic waves within a force-free electrodynamics (FFE) framework, specifically focusing on the linearized evolution of electric and magnetic fields around a stationary, stationary FFE solution. We derive a general set of linearized equations governing this evolution and apply them to the specific case of a stationary, axisymmetric FFE solution featuring a current sheet at the equator. Our analysis reveals that the magnetic field strength $B$ and electric field strength $E$ are perturbed by a factor of $B-E = \mathcal{O}(\epsilon)$, where $\epsilon$ represents the perturbation amplitude. Consequently, the difference between the fields decays over time, following a power law of $\sim t^{-1}$. This decay rate is consistent with numerical simulations. Furthermore, we demonstrate that the decay rate of the difference between the fields is proportional to the ratio of the difference between the fields to the magnetic field strength, i.e., $||E-B||/||E|| \sim t^{-1}$. This decay rate is consistent with numerical simulations. Finally, we discuss the implications of these findings for the stability of FFE solutions.

This study examines the Schrödinger's cat thought experiment by analyzing the temporal evolution of the cat-qubit state within Schrödinger's original framework. It demonstrates that the cat exists in both a superposition of states and an incoherent mixture of dead and alive conditions. Furthermore, the analysis extends to the cat oscillator, a system where the oscillation mode is coupled with a qubit comprising two energy levels.

This paper examines minimal periodic decomensions for the permutation $\sigma = 3214$, demonstrating that Szabados's conjecture holds true for these cases only when the patterns are uncomplicated. The findings also reveal a connection between the difficulty of solving the conjecture and the intricacy of the patterns.

This paper investigates the geometric characteristics of metric spaces derived from the growth trajectory of the growth function associated with the Gromov–Hausdorff distance within the set of isometry classes of bounded metric spaces. We demonstrate that, for a specific subset of this growth function, we can deduce the dimension of the space, and we also establish findings concerning the space's compactness and the finiteness of the Hausdorff-compactness constant.

This study examines the resolvent approximation for elliptic operators in divergence form, $L = -\nabla\cdot(a\nabla\cdot)$, which depend on a small parameter $\varepsilon$. We establish that the resolvent approximation error is of order $O(\varepsilon^2)$, provided that the coefficient $a(x/\varepsilon)$ possesses only a single spatial dimension of regularity. This finding is significant as it eliminates the need for the higher regularity (typically $H^3$) that was previously required in the literature. Furthermore, we present an explicit formula for the resolvent's second-order remainder, which facilitates the derivation of higher-order expansions.

Dialogue state tracking (DST) is a critical component of modern conversational agents, yet current methods often struggle with diverse and dynamic language contexts. This paper introduces a novel framework that utilizes formal dialogue states to enhance tracking performance. We propose a new DST model that integrates the strengths of both multi-task learning and DST control approaches. Specifically, we define dialogue states as a set of semantic tags, where each tag is represented by a specific semantic role. We employ a dual-task learning architecture that incorporates a semantic role classifier to predict these semantic roles alongside a DST model. This multi-task learning strategy enables the model to learn a more robust representation of dialogue states. Furthermore, we implement a DST control mechanism that leverages predicted semantic roles to guide the DST model, ensuring that its output aligns with the model's internal understanding of the dialogue state. Empirical results on the MultiWOZ benchmark demonstrate that our method surpasses existing state-of-the-art baselines.

This paper introduces Smt-Switch, a framework designed to enhance the performance of applications relying on Satisfiability Modulo Theory (SMT) solvers. The system leverages the ability of modern processors to cache frequently accessed memory locations, thereby reducing the time spent invoking external SMT solvers. Smt-Switch employs a lightweight, low-overhead mechanism to identify and cache reusable subproblems, which are then resolved locally on the host machine. Experimental results demonstrate that Smt-Switch significantly accelerates the execution of various applications, including model checkers, theorem provers, and software verification tools.

This study introduces a new technique for approximating eigenvalues and eigenvectors of the Schrödinger equation, termed Orthogonal Polynomial Projection Quantization (OPPQ). The method leverages the orthogonality of polynomial families to project the Hamiltonian onto a finite-dimensional matrix space, solving the resulting eigenvalue problem. We demonstrate that for quasi-exactly solvable (QES) states, the method maintains stability and converges to exact eigenvalues and eigenvectors as the matrix dimension increases. Conversely, for non-QES states, OPPQ exhibits instability, with the magnitude of this instability growing as the basis size expands. We also establish a theoretical link between the instability of non-QES states and the presence of QES eigenpairs within the spectrum. Furthermore, the method is applied to a range of exactly and quasi-exactly solvable systems, as well as to a model of the hydrogen atom subjected to a strong magnetic field.

This paper introduces a novel technique for adapting a Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) to a fixed computational budget by altering its input resolution. The method's core concept involves training the network on a dataset featuring variable input resolutions, thereby enabling the model to dynamically adjust its input resolution during inference. We demonstrate that this strategy allows the network to achieve a specific computational limit while maintaining a constant number of parameters and retaining its original accuracy. Furthermore, we apply this approach to transfer learning scenarios, showing that it facilitates the adaptation of pretrained models to different input resolutions without compromising the model's size.

This study examines the influence of a companion star's dynamical condition on the granular activity of a binary star's surface. We introduce a novel model of granular dynamics that incorporates the effects of magnetic fields and tidal forces. Our findings indicate that the secondary component's state can induce significant alterations in the structure of the photosphere's granulation. Furthermore, we explore the implications of these tidal effects on the evolution of magnetic fields and the generation of chemical abundance irregularities.

We investigate the formation of charged scalar clouds surrounding charged black holes within Einstein-Maxwell-scalar theory, specifically examining a complex scalar field governed by a self-interacting potential. Our findings indicate that these clouds can exist in both Reissner-Nordstr\"om and Kerr-Newman spacetimes. Furthermore, we determine their existence regions in parameter space and analyze their stability under linear perturbations.

This study examines the mixing between active and sterile neutrinos within a framework where sterile states are treated as Majorana fermions. The analysis focuses on the distinctive features of the resulting neutrino mass matrix, specifically the connection between the CP-violating phases and the signs of the active neutrino masses. The work also investigates the implications of these findings for both active-sterile mixing and neutrinoless double-beta decay.

This paper introduces a new denoising approach for 3D point clouds that leverages the concept of clean-noise disentanglement. The proposed method utilizes a Convolutional Variational Autoencoder (CVAE) to separate clean features from noisy ones. The core of this framework is the CVAD Denoising Feature (CVAD F) module, which employs a self-attention mechanism to capture long-range dependencies and utilizes the CVAE's latent space to distinguish between clean and noisy components. The clean feature extracted by the CVAD F module is subsequently refined by the PointNet++ network to generate the final denoised output. Experimental results demonstrate that this method achieves superior performance compared to existing state-of-the-art denoising techniques.

We demonstrate that for recovering a vector with sparsity $k$ from $n$ measurements, the matrix dimension $n$ must grow at least as $\Omega(k \log^2 n)$. This result is derived by establishing a lower bound on the number of rows in the measurement matrix $A$ required to guarantee $k$-sparse recovery, employing a novel method based on the geometric properties of convex polytopes. The upper bound on $n$ is tight up to a logarithmic factor. We further provide a constructive framework for creating such matrices, which is applicable to various algorithms, including LASSO, $\ell_1$ methods, and the nullspace approach.

Union and union and intersection types are a common feature in functional programming languages, yet they often introduce significant complexity, particularly in type inference. While existing research has largely focused on first-order systems, higher-order contexts remain underexplored. This paper introduces a calculus for function types that focuses on higher-order union and intersection types. We demonstrate that our approach maintains desirable characteristics, including decidability and confluence. Furthermore, we establish that our system can be integrated seamlessly with the standard simply-typed lambda calculus.

In recent years, reinforcement learning has achieved significant success in tackling complex tasks, yet it remains plagued by the challenge of inefficient learning. While numerous studies have explored the use of intrinsic motivation alongside extrinsic rewards to enhance training, the impact of reward magnitude on this process remains ambiguous. This paper investigates the relationship between reward size and learning efficiency within the context of the Curiosity-driven A3C (Curiosity-AC) framework. We introduce a novel approach that integrates both intrinsic and extrinsic signals to guide the agent's learning, utilizing a reward scaling method to dynamically adjust the strength of the curiosity signal. Experimental results indicate that this scaling strategy outperforms static approaches, demonstrating superior performance in training the agent.

This study investigates the oscillatory dynamics of a particle within a one-dimensional anharmonic potential, employing a perturbative expansion of the renormalized frequency in terms of the expansion coefficients. The analysis is conducted across two perturbation regimes: perturbations in the amplitude and in the velocity. The perturbation velocity approach is applied to a particle oscillating within a time-dependent harmonic well, whereas the amplitude method addresses a particle in a time-independent anharmonically corrected potential. The perturbations in the potential are treated using perturbation theory, with the resulting differential equations solved via the Magnus expansion. The findings demonstrate that the renormalized frequency exhibits a nonlinear dependence on the expansion coefficients.

We investigate the infrared dynamics of two-point correlation functions in gravity theories featuring a finite action boundary condition, specifically focusing on the exchange of graviton instantons. Our analysis reveals that the exchange of instantons with varying topological charges produces non-local contributions to the two-point functions, which manifest as phase factors dependent on the separation distance. We demonstrate that in the gravity theory, these instantonic contributions are governed by the finite action boundary condition, whereas in the dual field theory, they correspond to the exchange of a topological sector. Furthermore, we examine the consistency of the finite action boundary condition with the existence of asymptotic symmetries, and we show that the finite action boundary condition leads to a non-trivial modification of the asymptotic symmetry algebra.

This study examines the behavior of users who had their Twitter accounts suspended, aiming to determine if they are more likely to reoffend compared to active users. By analyzing a dataset of 1.4 million suspended accounts, we found that suspended users exhibit significantly higher rates of rule violations than their non-suspended counterparts. Additionally, we investigated the longevity of account suspensions and the effectiveness of the platform's content moderation. Our results indicate that rule violations persist over time, and while suspensions effectively halt such behavior temporarily, a substantial portion of users continue to violate rules after being returned to the platform.

The LHCb experiment, situated at the CERN facility, is dedicated to investigating the CP violation and rare decay processes of beauty and charm quarks. This article details the anticipated performance of LHCb under the operational conditions of the High-Luminosity LHC (HL-LHC) upgrade, which will commence in 2026. Furthermore, we examine the potential for LHCb to contribute to hadron-hadron collisions and discuss the implications for future proposals to enhance the accelerator design.

Neural networks are frequently trained on datasets containing noisy labels, a challenge that has driven the development of ensemble modeling to enhance robustness and accuracy. This study investigates how to construct ensembles specifically for classification tasks plagued by uncertain label annotations. We introduce a method that leverages soft labels—representing the distribution of class probabilities for each sample—to generate multiple hard label variants. These derived datasets are subsequently used to train individual neural networks, with the final prediction derived from an ensemble average across the outputs of all models. Our approach is evaluated on the widely recognized CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100 benchmarks, which feature artificially corrupted labels. The results demonstrate that the proposed ensemble strategy significantly outperforms single-model training and achieves superior results compared to existing state-of-the-art methods.

This study introduces a V2X resource allocation framework that prioritizes vehicles based on their proximity to high-risk crash zones. The process begins by clustering vehicles into groups and allocating resources to each group, followed by distributing specific resources to individual vehicles within those clusters. The cluster formation is modeled as a clustering problem, while the resource assignment for each group is formulated as a multiple access channel optimization task. The paper presents a solution to the channel optimization problem, which is proven to yield a Pareto-optimal solution. Furthermore, resources for individual vehicles are assigned using a weighted round-robin strategy, where weights are determined by the vehicle's location relative to the cluster's center. Theoretical analysis demonstrates that this proposed mechanism more effectively prioritizes vehicles near high-crash-risk clusters compared to conventional methods.

The widespread integration of artificial intelligence (AI) into daily life has heightened concerns regarding the explainability and equity of these systems. To address these issues, researchers have developed various frameworks for measuring fairness across different contexts. This paper introduces a novel metric designed to assess the fairness of machine learning models. It accomplishes this by quantifying the degree of disconnection between the distribution of sensitive attributes and the characteristics of data clusters. The proposed metric is grounded in the concept that the association between cluster characteristics and sensitive attributes should be negligible. Furthermore, we demonstrate that this new measure aligns with prior fairness definitions and theoretical findings, while also offering greater flexibility and interpretability.

Feature toggles are widely used to isolate and decouple development tasks, yet their impact on branch merge rates remains unclear. This study examines how toggles influence merge timing within a dataset of 1,099 software projects, comparing branches with and without their usage. The findings indicate that feature toggles accelerate the merge process, reducing the average branch lifespan by 13.5%. This effect is particularly pronounced in projects with fewer than 100 contributors, where the average duration drops by 20%. Additionally, we analyzed the reasons behind extended branch lifespans, identifying that complex feature toggles require more time to activate toggles, and that merge delays are common when features are not yet ready for integration. These insights can assist developers in better understanding the trade-offs between adopting feature toggles and branch longevity.

This study examines the link between the conservation of enstrophy in the 2D Navier-Stokes equations and accidental symmetry, demonstrating that such symmetry is not an intrinsic property but rather an approximation valid only at the coarsest scales of the system. Furthermore, we explore the relationship between this symmetry and the emergence of a boundary layer at the domain's edge, revealing that the symmetry is even more tenuous than previously thought. Ultimately, these results offer new perspectives on the connection between conserved quantities and symmetries within partial differential equations.

This paper introduces a visualization technique for attention maps derived from trained convolutional neural networks. We propose the Maximum Attention Visualization (MAV), which highlights the input regions where attention weights reach their peak. By revealing which specific features the network focuses on, MAV complements existing visualization methods that utilize gradients to determine regions of interest. We demonstrate that the regions identified by MAV align with those selected by human annotators, thereby proving its effectiveness. Additionally, we show that combining MAV with gradient-based visualization enhances the accuracy of object localization.

Political bias significantly influences the anticipated outcomes of peace negotiations and armed conflicts. This study proposes a novel framework for representing political bias, which models the bias as a set of weighted features derived from the bias's textual content. By leveraging Natural Language Processing (NLP) techniques to extract weighted features from the bias text, we assign a numerical weight to each feature, with higher values indicating a stronger association with the bias. This approach enables the representation of political bias as a vector of weighted features, which can subsequently be utilized to predict the bias's impact on war and peace outcomes. We have developed a comprehensive dataset of political bias extracted from Wikipedia pages and evaluated our proposed method on this data. Experimental results demonstrate that our approach effectively captures the nuances of political bias, which can then be leveraged to forecast the effects of bias on conflict outcomes.

This study presents a neural model of sentence processing that utilizes neural networks to encode a computational graph. We demonstrate that the model successfully captures the primary psycholinguistic findings regarding how humans process and comprehend sentences. Specifically, the model replicates the effects of filler filling, the binding of thematic roles, and the facilitation observed when sentence constituents align with prior context. Notably, the model reproduces these effects without relying on specialized mechanisms for sentence processing. Instead, the binding effects emerge naturally from the network's architecture, which is designed to represent the graph. We further show that the overlapping neural patterns associated with linking fillers to their corresponding thematic roles indicate that humans leverage neural representations of the graph to process both thematic roles and fillers concurrently.

The detection of neutrinos from binary black hole mergers is anticipated to be feasible during the next few years of Advanced LIGO and Virgo operations. Such a discovery would enable the triangulation of gravitational wave event triggers with angular precision ranging from 1 to 10 degrees. This level of accuracy is sufficient to narrow down the search area for electromagnetic counterparts to a manageable size. This study investigates how angular resolution in neutrino data influences the efficiency of identifying these counterparts. We demonstrate that angular accuracy can be enhanced by leveraging the time-of-arrival information of the constituent neutrino events. Furthermore, we detail a method for optimizing angular resolution by analyzing the temporal distribution of detected neutrinos. This approach is illustrated using simulated data from the GW170817 event, where the time-of-arrival distribution of neutrinos from the source was modeled.

This study investigates the impact of the primary mirror's surface quality on the performance of the adaptive optics (AO) system within the 3.6-meter Canada-France-Hawaii Telescope (CFHT). We introduce a novel method to quantify the spatial power spectral density (PSD) of the primary mirror by analyzing the residual PSD in the AO wavefront sensor (WFS) signal. This approach is applicable to any existing AO system, provided it utilizes a Shack-Hartmann WFS and employs a laser guide star. We demonstrate that the PSD amplitude in the WFS is governed by two factors: the PSD of the laser guide star itself and the PSD of the primary mirror. By isolating the star's PSD component, we successfully derived the primary mirror's PSD. We also developed a technique to estimate the PSD of the guide star by utilizing the AO system's natural guide star (NGS) mode, which relies on the NGS's own seeing conditions. This NGS-based natural seeing data allows for the separation of the two PSD components. We validated this method using the CFHT's AO system, which operates in both NGS and laser guide star modes. We confirmed that the spatial PSD amplitude in the primary mirror increases as mirror seeing worsens.

The r2SCAN density functional is applied to investigate phonon dispersions in rutile TiO$_2$, anatase TiO$_2$, and cubic SrTiO$_3$. This approach utilizes the functional's robust description of both structural and electronic properties, combined with density functional perturbation theory, to accurately model these systems. The resulting phonon dispersions align well with experimental data and previous theoretical predictions, demonstrating that r2SCAN is a dependable tool for predicting material properties.

This work establishes a framework for computing coverability sets of Very-WSTS (Specific Weighted Transition System) based on an extended, symbolic, and abstractly defined notion of "betweenness." By leveraging this generalized concept, we generalize the computation of coverability sets, previously established for unweighted systems, to the weighted domain. Our approach extends the traditional coverability graph to the coverability tree, enabling the representation of coverability sets as a collection of intervals. We demonstrate the applicability of this method to various very WSTS models, including weighted Petri nets, weighted Pushdown Automata, weighted Pushdown Automata, and weighted Pushdown Automata, and show how these concepts apply to weighted Petri nets, pushdown automata, and weighted pushdown systems.

This study examines the variability of active galactic nuclei (AGN) using data from the Zwicky Transient Facility (ZTF) and the Sloan Digital Sky Survey (SDSS). We introduce a novel methodology that leverages the ZTF's extensive time coverage to investigate long-term AGN variability, addressing the limitations of SDSS data regarding the latter half of the 2010s. By applying a newly developed Bayesian framework, we successfully model the heteroscedastic uncertainties inherent in ZTF observations. Our results indicate that the majority of AGN exhibit significant variability, with only a minority remaining constant. Furthermore, we observe a correlation between variability and black hole mass, a trend that aligns with findings from SDSS. Finally, we demonstrate that our approach is robust against contamination from quasars and supernovae, and we provide an open-source Python package designed to facilitate future research on AGN variability.

Quantum Darwinism (QD) serves as a framework for understanding how objective classical reality emerges from quantum systems, offering a novel approach to the measurement problem. This paper introduces a QD-inspired algorithm designed to reconstruct the pointer state of a quantum target using only classical information acquired from multiple environmental probes. The proposed method, Quantum Darwinism Reconstruction (QDR), is demonstrated to be highly effective for both pure and mixed target states. Additionally, the study explores the relationship between the quantum mutual information shared across all probes and the fidelity of the reconstructed pointer state.

This paper introduces a novel approach to analyzing the reachable set of discrete-time dynamical systems by leveraging principles from convex geometry. The core concept involves approximating the reachable set with ellipsoidal bounds, utilizing methods for estimating the convex hulls of ellipsoids to achieve this. The study derives sufficient conditions that ensure the reachable set is contained within a specific ellipsoid, and it also presents a procedure for calculating the tightest ellipsoidal enclosure. The paper concludes with numerical examples that illustrate the utility of these new findings.

This study introduces SAINT, a novel architecture for processing tabular data that integrates the strengths of both attention mechanisms and neural networks. By employing a multi-head self-attention mechanism on a sequence of features, the model effectively captures intricate relationships among variables. We evaluate SAINT across diverse regression and classification tasks, including credit scoring, customer churn prediction, and fraud detection. Our results demonstrate that SAINT consistently outperforms leading machine learning methods, such as XGBoost and LightGBM, in terms of predictive accuracy. Additionally, the model exhibits superior interpretability, a critical advantage for decision-making in fields like finance and healthcare.

Transfer learning is a technique that leverages knowledge from source domains to enhance performance in target domains, with its efficacy heavily dependent on the similarity between these domains. This study introduces a new method for assessing the degree of similarity between domains in image classification tasks. We utilize a pre-trained neural network to extract features from images and apply a clustering algorithm to these features to determine the similarity of the source and target domains. Our approach was tested on the ImageCLEF dataset, which contains images from various categories. Our findings indicate that the proposed method successfully captures the similarity of the domains, thereby aiding in the selection of the most appropriate source domains for transfer learning.

This study examines the restoration of chiral symmetry in the chiral limit within the framework of the Nambu–Jona-Lasinio model, utilizing the non-perturbative approach of the stochastic quantization method. We employ the lattice technique to discretize the chiral four-fermion interaction, thereby enabling the direct numerical calculation of fermion correlation functions. Our findings indicate that the system exhibits chiral symmetry breaking characterized by a non-vanishing fermion mass and the emergence of a massless Nambu–Goldstone boson.

This study presents a search for dark matter produced in association with a bottom-quark pair ($b$-quark pair) using proton-proton collision data from the CMS experiment at the CERN LHC, recorded at a center-of-mass energy of 13 TeV and an integrated luminosity of 35.9 fb$^{-1}$. The analysis targets a simplified model where dark matter interacts with the Standard Model solely via a mediator decaying into a $b$-quark pair. The study examines both the $b$-quark pair and top-quark pair channels, employing a cut-based approach to identify signal events. No significant excess above the Standard Model background is observed. Consequently, 95% confidence level upper limits on the dark matter cross section are established for both channels, with values of 0.010 pb and 0.0040 pb for the $b$-quark pair channel, respectively, at a dark matter mass of 100 GeV.

Concept location is a critical yet time-intensive phase in software development, often requiring developers to manually search through vast codebases to find specific definitions and implementations. This paper introduces a novel method to automate locating concepts by integrating crowd-sourced knowledge with existing deep learning models. We present a new dataset comprising over 100,000 crowd-contributed concepts, and our experimental results demonstrate that leveraging this data significantly outperforms state-of-the-art approaches. Furthermore, our analysis reveals that crowd contributions offer valuable insights for refining deep learning models used in this task.

This paper introduces a block-diagonal preconditioner for the efficient numerical solution of complex systems arising from the linearization of the compressible Navier-Stokes equations using the discontinuous Galerkin method. The preconditioner is designed to achieve optimal convergence rates regardless of polynomial degree, time step size, or mesh resolution. Additionally, its implementation is straightforward, requiring only the modification of the solver settings.

Summarizing dialogue is challenging because of its intricate structure, which often includes discourse relationships between utterances. This study introduces a new approach to abstractive dialogue summarization that leverages these discourse relations. We propose a model utilizing a graph neural network to integrate utterance dependencies into the summary generation process. Our approach employs a graph construction method based on local and global features to determine how to connect utterances via specific connectives. We also implement a graph attention mechanism to incorporate these dependency relations into the encoding of utterances. Furthermore, we develop a decoding strategy that ensures consistency of discourse relations throughout the summary. Evaluated on the multi-utterance subset of the multi-domain DialogueSummary dataset, our method outperforms existing baselines by 2.4 BLEU score.

This study introduces a deep learning approach for determining the Doppler broadening of nuclear cross-sections, utilizing thermal expansion data alongside temperature values. The proposed neural network architecture employs a multi-layer structure with a linear activation function in the hidden layer, utilizing a Leaky Rectified Linear Unit (ReLU) for the output layer. The model was trained using resonance datasets from uranium-235 and plutonium-239 obtained via the SAMMY code. Evaluation against standard methods demonstrates that the deep learning technique achieves accuracy comparable to the BRIT code for calculating broadening effects.

This paper introduces $(n + 1)$-pre-Lie algebras defined by $(n + 1)$-coactions of $n$-pre-Lie algebras, which are shown to encompass generalized $n$-pre-Lie algebras. We provide a corresponding definition for $(n+1)$-Nijenhuis operators based on these structures and investigate their relationship with $n$-pre-Lie coinvolves. Furthermore, we define $n$-pre-Lie F-manifolds, present an associated definition for $(n + 1)$-pre-Lie F-manifolds, and examine how $(n + 1)$-pre-Lie F-manifolds relate to $(n + 1)$-pre-Lie coinvolves. We also define $(n + 1)$-pre-Lie comultiples, establish their fundamental properties, and demonstrate their relationship to $(n + 1)$-pre-Lie subalgebras. Finally, we define $(n + 1)$-pre-Lie coinvolves, establish their basic properties, and demonstrate their relationship to $(n + 1)$-pre-Lie coinvolves.

This paper introduces a scheduling framework designed to balance the throughput requirements of real-time and non-realtime users. By integrating a random access mechanism for real-time users with a scheduling algorithm for non-realtime users, the system ensures a fair distribution of resources. The proposed scheme employs a weighted sum of throughputs, where weights reflect the priority of each user category, and optimizes the scheduling algorithm to maximize this combined metric. The maximum throughput is achieved by identifying the optimal power allocation for non-realtime users, which is solved using a bisection search. Simulation results demonstrate that the real-time throughput improves by 10% compared to simpler approaches, while the overall system throughput increases by 15%.

This study addresses whether the approximation of an entire function via its translation orbit depends on the type of convergence. The authors demonstrate that for the convergence to hold uniformly, a significantly stricter condition is required than that for pointwise approximation. These conditions relate to specific properties of the distribution of zeros of the entire function under the translation operator. Furthermore, it is established that for all exponential order entire functions, pointwise approximation always occurs, though the rate of convergence is notably slow.

The rheological behavior of disordered materials is significantly influenced by their microstructural characteristics. This study investigates how altering these properties affects rheology in a simplified framework: a system of soft spheres confined within a rigid, disordered matrix. We demonstrate that the rheological response can be effectively tuned by modifying the materials' microstructural attributes. Specifically, we show that a transition from a jammed to a flowing state can be achieved solely by adjusting the confining matrix's porosity, without any changes to the confining forces or the system's temperature.

Continual learning is vital for object detection, especially for robotic and autonomous systems operating in dynamic environments. However, current research predominantly focuses on classification, leaving object detection largely unexplored. This paper introduces a novel framework for continual detection that integrates object detection with state-of-the-art continual learning techniques. We propose a new object detection model featuring a shared backbone and two heads: one for detection and one for classification. To enhance object detection performance, we utilize the object classifier head to generate auxiliary class labels for every bounding box, thereby enriching the training data. Additionally, we employ a dynamic weight-sharing mechanism to mitigate catastrophic forgetting in the shared backbone. Experiments on the COCO dataset demonstrate that our approach outperforms existing continual detection methods, achieving improvements in both accuracy and the mitigation of forgetting.

We examine the medium-enhanced production of quark-antiquark pairs in ultra-relativistic heavy-ion collisions using the Boltzmann transport equation. Our analysis indicates that although this production mechanism is non-negligible only when the partonic cross section remains large, its impact on the overall multiplicity is minor.

We introduce DivCAM, a novel data augmentation method designed to train neural networks for domain generalization. Drawing on the concept of domain confusion, DivCAM creates diverse augmentations by mixing different source domains. This approach is straightforward to implement and computationally efficient, as it relies solely on pixel-wise operations. Our experiments demonstrate that DivCAM significantly outperforms existing state-of-the-art techniques across various domains and tasks.

Blockchain technology has emerged as a promising solution for enhancing the security and decentralization of internet infrastructure. However, existing implementations often suffer from a lack of standardization, which hinders their ability to address specific challenges within the internet ecosystem. This paper introduces a platform-independent blockchain designed to empower agent models in internet infrastructure by providing programmable capabilities. We present a formal model of our proposed system, along with a corresponding implementation built on the Ethereum Virtual Machine (EVM). This model facilitates the development of a novel, programmable framework for applying blockchain technology to agent-based games. We validate our approach by applying the model to a simple game of Chicken, demonstrating how it can be used to create a provably secure mechanism for distributing game outcomes.

This study examines the viability of both exponential and polynomial $ \alpha$-attractor models by analyzing their consistency with cosmological observations. Our findings indicate that the exponential model aligns more effectively with the data than the polynomial counterpart. Furthermore, we examine the relationship between the spectral index and tensor-to-scalar ratio for these models, revealing that the exponential model can simultaneously satisfy observational limits on both parameters, whereas the polynomial model cannot.

This paper outlines a performance evaluation of an end-to-end AI pipeline, specifically the automated detection of COVID-19 cases. It examines the impact of various optimization techniques on both the computational and inferential performance throughout the pipeline. Our findings reveal that optimization can deliver up to a 100% improvement in quality and a 30% reduction in inference time. Additionally, we demonstrate that utilizing a single GPU can process up to 100,000 CT scans per hour.

This study evaluates the type 2 error rates of three methods—Bayes Factors, High Density Interval (HDI) Region of Practical Equivalence (ROPE), and frequentist equivalence tests—when applied to equivalence testing. We simulated data from a two-sample t-test with unequal variances, comparing the performance of these approaches at significance levels of 0.05 and 0.10 calibrated to a type 1 error rate of 0.05 for the Frequentist test. Additionally, we calibrated Baye's Factor thresholds to achieve a 0.05 posterior probability of equivalence. The results indicate that type 2 error rates for Baye's Factor, HDI-ROPE, and the frequentist equivalence test are generally comparable when set to identical type 1 error rates, though the frequentist approach tends to be slightly more conservative. Furthermore, we simulated data from a two-sample t-test with equal variances to assess the robustness of the findings.

This study introduces a novel adversarial training approach designed to enhance the reception quality of visual data within the framework of digital semantic communication. The methodology involves generating adversarial examples at the receiver end, which are subsequently fed back to the transmitter to refine the semantic encoder. This process effectively mitigates the influence of adversarial noise on received imagery, thereby elevating image fidelity. The proposed technique is validated using the semantic image transmission variant of the semantic image compression (SICC) framework, demonstrating significant performance gains. The findings indicate that this adversarial training method can enhance peak signal-to-signal ratio (PSNR) by up to 1.5 dB and improve Fréchet Inception Distance (FID) scores by as much as 15.0%.

Skew is a prevalent issue in data processing, where uneven data distribution across processing units causes significant performance degradation. While numerous frameworks have been developed to address skew, they often rely on specific data distribution patterns, limiting their adaptability. This paper introduces Reshape, a new framework designed to dynamically detect skew and automatically mitigate it. Reshape operates by aggregating multiple fine-grained tasks into a coarser granularity, allowing it to overcome processor limitations and balance workload distribution. The result is a substantial improvement in execution efficiency, achieving up to 10x speedup compared to traditional methods.

This work extends the concept of a modal logic framework to encompass comonads, adjunctions, and specific functors. It establishes that comonads and adjunctions each yield a modal interior operator, quantifying information loss through the respective Koszul duals. Additionally, we identify a category of modal logics that includes both Tarski and Heyting varieties, offering a novel generalization of the latter. Finally, we demonstrate that modal Kripke semantics can be generalized to these broader contexts, utilizing the associated interior operators.

This paper introduces a novel network autoregression model that integrates a graphically assisted Chinese restaurant process (CRP) to jointly model the graph and response variables. By leveraging the graph's topological structure, the CRP facilitates the clustering of nodes, thereby enhancing the interpretability of network effects and mitigating the computational burden associated with large-scale networks. We demonstrate that this model possesses a closed-form maximum likelihood estimator and establish theoretical convergence rates for the maximum likelihood estimator under specific regularity conditions. Furthermore, we illustrate how the proposed graphically assisted CRP can be extended to broader hierarchical frameworks, such as graphically assisted hierarchical Bayesian models. We show that a Bayesian extension of the CRP-based network autoregression yields significant gains in statistical inference, particularly in recovering true network effects and recovering the underlying graph structure. Additionally, we present a new Bayesian extension of the CRP that enables the model to handle latent covariates. Finally, the proposed methodology is validated through a simulation study and a real-world application involving the analysis of student performance data from the National Assessment of Educational Progress (NAEP).

SciFact represents a pioneering dataset designed for scientific claim verification, comprising 10,000 claims extracted from Wikipedia pages dedicated to scientific articles. Each claim is paired with a specific page URL intended to provide context for its validity. The dataset encompasses a wide variety of scientific disciplines and features a diverse array of claim types, ranging from those easily verifiable to highly complex ones. We have developed a baseline model that leverages both the claim text and the associated URL, utilizing them as inputs for a joint training approach. Our evaluation demonstrates that this baseline significantly surpasses existing state-of-the-art methods, underscoring the potential of scientific claims supported by contextual URLs.

This study introduces a technique for automatically segmenting the inner retinal layers in both normal and diseased retinal scans, facilitating the accurate identification of pathologies. The proposed method enhances compartmentalization of the posterior eye by integrating a novel approach to distinguish between the retinal pigment epithelium (RPE) and choroid, even in the presence of artifacts and noise. The workflow begins with a multi-scale analysis of the fundus image to generate a feature map, which is subsequently processed by a U-Net architecture to produce a preliminary segmentation. This output is then refined through a specialized post-processing step that leverages the distinct textural characteristics of the posterior layers to separate the RPE from the choroid. Experimental results demonstrate that the method achieves a Dice Similarity Coefficient (DSC) of 0.92 and a Mean Absolute Error (MAE) of 1.92 pixels, outperforming existing state-of-the-art techniques.

The assumption of static or homogeneous parameters in cognitive models is frequently criticized for overlooking the potential for temporal dynamics. This study introduces a new approach to model time-varying cognitive processes by applying a time-dependent transformation to the parameters of a standard linear model. This method is demonstrated through a case study of the well-known leaky competing accumulator model, which is adapted to account for changing parameters over time. The proposed framework is then contrasted with the conventional static model using a dataset from a Stroop task. Results indicate that the time-dependent model provides a superior fit to the data, thereby capturing temporal variations in cognitive processing.

This study introduces a fresh criterion for identifying Mersenne compositeness and utilizes it to establish two novel lower bounds for the size of Mersenne primes. Additionally, the paper derives two fresh upper bounds applicable to the smallest prime factor of Mersenne primes with two distinct forms. The research also establishes new lower bounds for the smallest prime factor of general integer powers.

We report observations of the [C ii] 158 $\mu$m and [O i] 63 $\mu$m lines for 10 starburst galaxies from the Herschel-ATLAS survey, including the extreme starburst NGC 6240. Our analysis reveals that the ratios of these emission lines are highly variable, with values ranging from 0.1 to 1.5. These ratios are generally lower than those found in local starburst galaxies, which typically exhibit ratios between 1.0 and 1.5. The observed ratios align with theoretical predictions for starburst galaxies with low-density molecular wind or circumgalactic gas reservoirs. Specifically, the [C ii] 158 $\mu$m emission in these systems is dominated by low-density gas, whereas the [O i] 63 $\mu$m emission primarily originates from high-density molecular gas. Additionally, we find that the [O i] 63 $\mu$m line is optically thick in these starburst galaxies.

This study investigates how annotators can enhance their consensus when labeling spoken language. We introduce a new framework that utilizes a Bayesian network to model the annotation process, integrating both utterance features and annotator-specific factors. This approach enables the identification of utterances likely to benefit from additional inter-annotator review, as well as the profiling of individual annotators to suggest specific clusters of data points they should examine to reach consensus with peers. We evaluated these methods on a dataset of 1,000 utterances annotated by five participants for emotion classification. Results indicate that our method significantly boosts annotator agreement without compromising data quality.

The study investigates the dispersal mechanisms of circumstellar discs around young stars, utilizing a sample of 1000 young stars from the Orion Nebula Cluster (ONC) with masses ranging from 0.1 to 10 solar masses. By analyzing the relationship between stellar mass and inner-disc lifetime, the authors find that the observed trend aligns with a dispersal mechanism driven by planet formation. This trend can be effectively reproduced using a model where the inner disc lifetime is directly linked to the time required for the first core to reach a critical mass of 10 Jupiter units. This proposed planet formation timescale is consistent with the observed disc lifetime distribution across the full mass range of the sample. Furthermore, the study suggests that the formation of a planetary core of 10 Jupiter units is a prerequisite for the onset of runaway gas accretion.

This study introduces a novel approach for generating high-order, multi-dimensional, unconditionally stable, and energy-conserving schemes for the linear wave equation. By modifying the method's coefficients, one can regulate numerical dissipation within the high-frequency domain.

This paper investigates the residue behaviors of a polaron situated within a Bose gas confined to a double-well potential, where the gas exhibits repulsive interactions. Our findings indicate that the polaron's nature and residue dynamics are significantly influenced by the size of the Bose gas trap. Specifically, the polaron undergoes a transition from a delocalized to a localized state as the trap size increases. Furthermore, the specific residue behaviors observed depend on the magnitude of both the Bose gas interaction and the trap size.

This study addresses the strategic logistics of pre-positioning relief supplies ahead of hurricanes by utilizing a Markov chain framework to model the stochastic nature of storm landfalls. The research establishes an optimization model aimed at maximizing the expected value of relief items upon demand realization, a task solved using dynamic programming. The resulting optimal policy is then implemented through a Markov decision process (MDP) via successive linear programming. The paper concludes with a case study applying the proposed model to the distribution of mobile kitchens in Florida, specifically targeting the state's most frequent landfall locations.

This study examines the gravitational-wave background (GWB) produced by a stochastic ensemble of inspiralling binary systems, specifically deriving and contrasting two approaches: a closed-form approximate formula and a numerical method. We find that the approximate analytic expression yields an accuracy of approximately 10% for typical PTA experiments, whereas the numerical approach achieves better than 1% precision. Additionally, we analyze how GWB parameters evolve with variations in the population's physical characteristics, such as binary mass distributions and orbital eccentricity. Our findings indicate that the numerical method's superior accuracy makes it the preferred choice for future gravitational-wave experiments.

This paper investigates Bayesian coordination games featuring multiple equilibria, where agents possess private information regarding the likelihood of each game form. We demonstrate that, under specific conditions, agents can successfully coordinate on distinct equilibria contingent upon the state. Our model is grounded in the "Bayesian persuasion" literature, as a principal can influence the game's state distribution to facilitate such coordination. We show that, under mild assumptions, the principal can achieve any Bayes correlated equilibrium, and we illustrate that these outcomes may yield superior results compared to standard contract mechanisms.

This study introduces a method for performing terahertz spectroscopy on aqueous solutions using a microfluidic coplanar waveguide (CPW) connected to a low-noise high-electron-mobility transistor (HEMT) detector. The microfluidic channel is integrated directly into the CPW, enabling the direct flow of liquids through the radiating element. This design allows for the precise measurement of liquid permittivity and loss tangent as a function of frequency, offering a distinct advantage over conventional spectrometers that rely on resonant cavities or waveguides. By utilizing a low-impedance transmission line, the system achieves a high signal-to-noise ratio, which is particularly beneficial for analyzing weakly absorbing liquids. The system's sensitivity is further enhanced by the HEMT's low-noise properties. As a demonstration, the method was used to measure the permittivity of water at 0.14 THz, yielding a result of 78.0 ± 0.5, which aligns well with the literature value of 78.5 ± 0.5.

This study introduces a novel framework for forecasting the risk of disease contagion by integrating environmental and human behavioral variables. The proposed methodology utilizes a deep learning architecture to forecast the density of susceptible and infected populations, thereby estimating the risk of transmission. The model is trained using data derived from a susceptible-infected-recovered (SIR) model, which serves as the foundation for the risk prediction. The research demonstrates that this data-driven approach can effectively incorporate various factors to forecast the risk of disease transmission. The study also compares the performance of this method against a traditional SIR model, revealing that the data-driven model offers superior predictive capabilities. The authors conclude that this data-driven methodology can enhance the accuracy of epidemic forecasting and provide valuable insights for public health officials in planning and mitigating the impact of outbreaks.

This study introduces a novel multi-phase framework based on the Smoothed Particle Hydrodynamics (SPH) method, utilizing a multi-resolution approach. By employing a variable resolution strategy, the model mitigates the issue of particle clustering in regions of high density. Furthermore, the approach integrates a multi-phase model capable of managing voids and handling multiphase flows with high density contrasts, while the use of a specific equation of state prevents the occurrence of spurious currents.

Nodal lines are one-dimensional topological structures in momentum space that are protected by symmetry and characterized by a non-trivial Chern number. While these lines are typically described as having a single dimensionality, they can be projected onto a two-dimensional plane, creating a loop that intersects itself at a node point. This work demonstrates that such a configuration can be engineered in a three-dimensional photonic crystal by utilizing a gyrotropic material. The resulting topology is confirmed through the observation of a non-zero Chern number and the presence of one-dimensional robust surface states.

The software development challenges associated with Monte Carlo event generators for high-luminosity physics are examined, with a particular focus on the complexities of simulating pile-up conditions.

This study investigates the relationship between molecular and atomic gas in the outer Galaxy by analyzing the distribution of molecular gas, as defined by the $^{12}$CO(1-0) line, across the region $L>30^\circ$ and $b=-5^\circ$ to $b=5^\circ$. Utilizing the 2MASS JHK survey, we identified 1,000,000,000,000,000,000,000,000,000,000,000,000,000,000,000,000,000,000,000,000,000,000,000,000,000,000,000,000,000,000,000,000,000,000,000,000,000,000,000,000,000,000,000,000,000,000,000,000,000,000,000,000,000,000,00

We introduce a novel framework for wage redistribution, grounded in a framework of consumer choice and evolutionary dynamics. The consumer choice game serves as a foundational model for evolutionary game theory, while the redistribution process is driven by evolutionary dynamics. The consumer choice game itself is analyzed through the lens of a master equation.

We investigate the impact of alignment interactions on active particle systems using a minimal model of active glasses. Our findings reveal that alignment induces a transition from disorder to order, characterized by a shift from shear-thickening to shear-thinning behavior. At elevated densities, increasing alignment strength triggers a transition from shear-thickening rheology to a state of solid-like elasticity. Conversely, at lower densities, this interaction competes with activity, progressively altering dynamics until activity is eventually suppressed, resulting in fluidization.

This study introduces a new task for geolocation: identifying an observer's position within an image using only visual cues. We developed a dataset of 1,000 images from Google Street View, each annotated with the camera's origin and the locations of 1,000 other points visible in the scene. These "locations" include landmarks, vehicles, and addresses, while "Locators" are humans tasked with finding the camera's origin among the annotated set. We developed a deep learning model to automate this process, achieving a 60% success rate compared to a 70% success rate for human Locators. Furthermore, we evaluated whether our system could infer the camera's origin from a single image, achieving 40% accuracy against a 50% accuracy for human Locators.

This study introduces a method for selecting frequency bands in machinery monitoring that surpasses the capabilities of conventional approaches. The approach is founded on a novel metric called the Band Relevance Factor (BRF), which quantifies the connection between a specific frequency band and the fault condition of a machine. The proposed BRF leverages the mutual information between the Hilbert spectrum of a signal's segment and its empirical mode decomposition (EMD) residue. The paper demonstrates the method's effectiveness through two case studies: monitoring a bearing in a rotating machine and analyzing a gearbox.

The superconducting coherence lengths ($\xi$) for the compounds CaPtSi$_3$ and CaIrSi$_3$ were determined using the critical field anisotropy method, which relies on the temperature dependence of the upper critical field $H_{c2}(T)$. The $H_{c2}(T)$ data were fitted to the Werthamer-Clogston-Parisi (WCL) theory, which accounts for strong spin-orbit coupling and the proximity of the Zeeman limit. The results indicate that CaPtSi$_3$ possesses a shorter coherence length than CaIrSi$_3$ across all three principal crystallographic axes. Additionally, the coherence lengths for CaPtSi$_3$ align well with those of its analogue, Ca$_3$PtSi$_3$, suggesting that the substitution of Ca with Ca3 does not significantly alter these parameters.

The Hamilton-Jacobi-Bellman (HJB) equation, central to optimal control theory, is typically formulated as a partial differential equation (PDE) that is challenging to solve using traditional methods due to the curse of dimensionality. This study introduces a novel deep learning framework to address the HJB equation, leveraging the inherent structure of the equation to significantly lower the number of parameters required in the neural network. By utilizing a neural network to represent the value function, the method reformulates the HJB problem into a nonlinear partial differential algebraic equation (pDPE) involving the Hamiltonian. A specialized neural network architecture is proposed to solve this pDPE, which incorporates the Hamiltonian as a constraint within the loss function. The approach is validated through two numerical examples, demonstrating its effectiveness.

Quantum computing holds the potential to significantly advance classical machine learning algorithms. This study introduces a quantum-enhanced supervised classification method that integrates a quantum neural network (QNN) with a support vector machine (SVM). The QNN is designed to learn from the SVM's predicted errors, thereby adjusting its internal parameters to generate more accurate outputs for the SVM. This collaborative approach enables the reinforcement of the SVM through the QNN. The proposed hybrid model is implemented on an IBM quantum processor and evaluated using the MNIST dataset. The results indicate that this quantum-inspired strategy surpasses the performance of standalone support vector machines.

This paper introduces a multi-layered energy modeling strategy for energy systems, utilizing both modeling and control perspectives to define system layers. It aims to enhance energy modeling by offering greater detail than conventional power flow analysis while maintaining computational efficiency. The approach is validated through a case study of a microgrid, demonstrating its ability to inform and refine control strategies.

This study introduces a deep learning approach for analyzing percolation states, utilizing the Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) to extract key features like density and correlation length. The CNN was trained on a dataset of percolation states generated via Monte Carlo simulations, specifically designed to identify the percolation threshold. The model's performance was validated using a separate test set, demonstrating that the CNN can accurately determine the percolation threshold for various two-dimensional binary image configurations.

The temperature-dependent proton resonance frequency shift serves as a non-invasive method for measuring core temperatures in reactors. This paper examines the proton resonance frequency shift in aqueous solutions, specifically those containing dissolved salts. The study investigates the impact of dissolved salts on the proton relaxation time and chemical shift of water, alongside the proton resonance frequency shift relative to temperature. The research further explores how the proton resonance frequency shift varies with salt concentration.

This study examines how disorder and non-uniformity influence superconducting fluctuations approaching the critical point in two-dimensional superconductors. We derive an analytical formula for the non-equilibrium local susceptibility, applicable to both inhomogeneous and disordered systems. This approach enables the calculation of the average local susceptibility across the entire system. Our findings indicate that introducing randomness and non-uniformity substantially modifies the fluctuation behavior near the transition.

We present an $O(n^2)$-time algorithm capable of $k$-median clustering for finite point sets in $\mathbb{R}^2$, provided $k$ is fixed. This result is achieved by adapting the technique from Berman and Vaidya (1999), which originally established an $O(kn^2)$-time algorithm for $k$-median on metric spaces. Subsequently, we extend this methodology to develop an $O(kn^{1.5})$-time algorithm for $k$-median clustering of finite point sets in $\mathbb{R}^3$.
